CampaignAssuranceIdempotencyKey.description:
Exactly one key is required. It must be non-empty valid UTF-8, contain
no control characters, and be at most 255 UTF-8 bytes. Reuse the same
key only for an exact retry of the same logical mutation. Campaign
Assurance also requires a UUID `request_id` for run creation and
finding decisions; the two identities serve different audit layers.
CampaignAssuranceIdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key

ConsentLedgerCursor.description:
Client-opaque keyset continuation returned as `next_cursor`. Its
HMAC-authenticated `base64url(payload).base64url(signature)` envelope
repeats the authenticated workspace, endpoint, a domain-separated keyed
exact-filter binding, recording-time watermark, PostgreSQL visibility
snapshot, and last row identity; the server combines that snapshot with
each row's database-owned top-level recording transaction identity.
This insert-visibility boundary excludes rows recorded by transactions
that were still active when the first page began, including
subtransactions, even if they commit before a continuation request. It
is not a cross-request repeatable-read snapshot: governed updates,
redactions, and deletions can change or remove older rows. Honest clients
cannot accidentally move a cursor
between the receipt, subject-history, or event endpoints or reuse it
after filters change. A dedicated server key authenticates the entire
envelope and prevents an offline dictionary test of the deprecated
subject-history email binding. It is a traversal token, not durable
consent evidence; tenant RLS remains the data boundary. The v1 envelope
has no embedded expiry, so acceptance is currently bounded by signing-key
lifecycle rather than a per-cursor TTL. Clients must retain it only for
the active traversal, and key rotation/overlap remains an explicit
release-lifecycle control.
Duplicate, empty, malformed, or oversized cursors are rejected. Treat
the value as opaque and return it unchanged; it can contain internal
database visibility metadata. Application logs and client telemetry
must redact it. Edge and access-log query governance remains a
deployment acceptance control.
ConsentLedgerCursor.name: cursor

ConsentLedgerLimit.description: Bounded page size. Omission selects 200; zero, signs, decimals, whitespace, and duplicate values are rejected.
ConsentLedgerLimit.name: limit

ConsentLedgerSince.description: Inclusive RFC3339 occurrence-time lower bound. The exact value is cursor-bound when present.
ConsentLedgerSince.name: since

ConversionTrackingKeyIdempotencyKey.description:
Optional high-entropy key scoped across this tenant's authenticated
mutation surface for 24 hours. Reuse it only for an exact retry of the
same method, escaped target (including query), and raw request body.
Successful and 4xx responses—including the plaintext site-key
response—are cached and replayable by administrators until expiry.
ConversionTrackingKeyIdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key

FederationChildIfMatch.description:
Exactly one strong validator for the child subscriber whose federation
graph is changing. Echo the `subscriber_version` or `ETag` from the
latest federation-list or subscriber response. Missing/empty,
wildcard, weak, and comma-list values fail closed with 428; a stale
token returns 412.
FederationChildIfMatch.name: If-Match

HelpdeskCursor.description:
Opaque AES-GCM token bound to tenant, route/kind, exact filters/order,
limit, version, a creation-window `as_of`, and a 15-minute expiry.
Return it unchanged and never log it. Rotation intentionally resets
active traversal; no previous-key overlap is currently advertised.
HelpdeskCursor.name: cursor

HelpdeskIfMatch.description:
Exactly one strong quoted validator returned in ETag. Use
`"absent"` only for the first complete config PUT. Wildcards, weak
validators, unquoted values, duplicate headers, and noncanonical
timestamps are rejected with 428; a stale valid value returns 412.
HelpdeskIfMatch.name: If-Match

HelpdeskInternalNoteIdempotencyKey.description:
Exactly one value is required. It must be 1–255 valid UTF-8 bytes,
have no leading/trailing whitespace, and contain no C0/C1, bidi, or
zero-width controls. It is durably bound to tenant, principal,
conversation, route, and request hash. Reuse only for the exact retry;
key/body mismatch returns `409 idempotency_key_conflict`.
HelpdeskInternalNoteIdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key

HelpdeskLimit.description: Page size. Unknown, repeated, signed, whitespace-padded, fractional, zero, and out-of-range values are rejected.
HelpdeskLimit.name: limit

HelpdeskResourceID.description: Lowercase canonical UUID with no surrounding whitespace.
HelpdeskResourceID.name: id

IdempotencyKey.description: Stable caller-generated key for exact mutation retries after an ambiguous response.
IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key

MCPInclude.description: Omit for strict official-MCP source classification; `all` includes other API-key traffic.

OutboundWebhookPlaygroundIdempotencyKey.description:
Exactly one caller-generated value is required. It must be 1–255 valid
UTF-8 bytes with no surrounding whitespace or control characters. Mint
it with `fire_id`, retain both through cancellation, and reuse this key
only with the byte-equivalent logical fire request. A different request
under the same key returns 422; a fire still crossing the receiver
boundary returns 409 and must be reconciled by `fire_id`.
OutboundWebhookPlaygroundIdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key

PrivacyIncidentIdempotencyKey.description:

surrounding whitespace it must be non-empty valid UTF-8, contain no
control characters, and be at most 255 UTF-8 bytes. Reuse it only for
an exact retry of the same method, target, and request body.
PrivacyIncidentIdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key

SmsInboxPhone.description: Canonical US/Canada E.164 conversation identity. Encode the leading plus in URLs.

object's `version` or `ETag`. Missing/empty, wildcard, weak, and

VerificationIdempotencyKey.description:
Exactly one opaque key is required. Its value is an exact request
identity and is used exactly as supplied. Leading or trailing
whitespace is invalid. The value must contain 1-255 bytes of valid UTF-8
and no control characters. Within its 24-hour HTTP replay window the
key is scoped to the authenticated tenant, principal replay scope, and
verification endpoint and must only be reused with the exact same request.
VerificationIdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key

SendingSettingsMutationBadRequest.description: The request was malformed or an Idempotency-Key was supplied to this deliberately non-replayable cap-control operation; settings were not changed.

SendingSettingsMutationConflict.description: The loaded settings revision is stale, another cap change already owns the tenant fence, or an active Deliverability Hub repair owns the installed cap; nothing committed.

Retry-After.description: Present as one second when another cap mutation owns the conservative fence.

SendingSettingsMutationCoordinationUnava.description:
Shared cap coordination was unavailable before commit, the durable
settings committed but Redis convergence remains fenced, or the
database commit outcome could not be proven. The exact body code and
outcome header distinguish these states; clients must reconcile rather
than blindly retry a committed or unknown outcome.

Retry-After.description: Minimum seconds before refreshing canonical settings and cap status.

X-Postwave-Sending-Cap-Outcome.description: Exact durable database/cap-coordination result for this request.

SendingSettingsMutationNotCommitted.description: The settings mutation did not commit.

SendingSettingsMutationOutcomeUnproven.description:
A server failure prevented a normal response. The optional mutation
outcome header is present only when the handler established an exact
phase result before the failure. It can prove no commit, a durable
commit with converged coordination, a durable commit still fenced, or
an unknown commit outcome still fenced. If the header is absent, the
outcome is ambiguous. Clients must never infer `not-committed` from the
500 status and must use read-only reconciliation before another write.

X-Postwave-Sending-Cap-Outcome.description: Optional exact mutation phase receipt. Absence leaves the outcome ambiguous.

error.message: A previous request with this Idempotency-Key is still processing. Retry after the Retry-After window.
Some provider requests may have completed before the batch failed. The batch was not retried to avoid duplicate charges.

VerificationIdempotencyConflict.description:
The exact request is still in progress, or a provider call crossed the
potentially billable boundary without returning a complete outcome.
In-progress requests return `idempotency_key_in_progress` plus
`Retry-After`. Uncertain provider outcomes return the deterministic
`verification_provider_outcome_ambiguous` response, which is retained
and replayed for the key's 24-hour lifetime so exact retries cannot
redispatch the provider call. A completed verification whose usage
accounting write cannot be confirmed similarly returns and replays
`verification_usage_outcome_ambiguous`.

Retry-After.description: Present for an in-progress request; minimum seconds before retrying it.

error.message: This Idempotency-Key was already used with a different verification request. Use a fresh key.

VerificationIdempotencyMismatch.description:

same tenant and verification endpoint. Use a fresh key for new input.

error.message: A previous request with this Idempotency-Key is still processing. Retry after the Retry-After window.

VerificationJobIdempotencyInProgress.description:
An exact bulk-job creation request using this Idempotency-Key is still
processing. Retry only the byte-identical request after the indicated
interval; no second job is created while the claim is pending.

Retry-After.description: Minimum seconds before retrying the exact request.

error.message: Async bulk verification is temporarily unavailable.

Returned once, on creation. Capture the token before discarding this
response; it cannot be retrieved later, and a lost token means minting a

A mandate as the list endpoint returns it. The bearer token is
deliberately absent — it exists only in the agent's memory and as a hash
on the server, so a list that could hand it back would make every reader
of this page able to act as the agent.

resources.description: What it may do those things to.

revoked_at.description: Set when a person withdrew the mandate, as distinct from it expiring or being spent.

uses_remaining.description: Calls left before the mandate is spent. Reaching zero ends it as surely as revoking does.

enabled.description: Whether scheduled execution is enabled; manual execution remains available.

has_active_run.description:
True while one durable manual or scheduled run owns this routine.
A routine with an active run cannot be started again, patched, or
deleted until that receipt becomes succeeded or failed.

require_approval.description: Whether generated drafts open a human approval gate.

Inert legacy storage returned only so an operator can explicitly

replaces the target, an empty string clears it, and omission or JSON

Empty string clears an inert legacy value; omission or null leaves
it unchanged. Any non-empty value is rejected with `422
unsupported_target_list`.

Per-week fraction of the signup cohort with the selected activity.
Weeks are measured from each subscriber's own signup timestamp.
Only fully matured cohort weeks are present; an immature trailing
week is omitted rather than serialized as zero.

apps/api/internal/handlers/audit.go.

event. The false value is omitted by the current handler.

write time. These are field NAMES, not values, and are

applies.

AIVS bundle.

AutomationLifecycleStageTrigger.description:
SUB-136 — one entry in an automation flow's `triggers` array that fires
when a subscriber transitions between lifecycle stages. When a
PUT /api/v1/subscribers/{id}/lifecycle actually changes the stage, the
gateway forwards a `subscriber_lifecycle_stage_changed` event (carrying
from_stage/to_stage) to the automation runtime, which matches it against
every active automation carrying a trigger of this type and fires the
entry node. An optional from_stage/to_stage narrows the match — e.g.
from_stage=opportunity + to_stage=customer fires only on that exact
transition. Omitting either filter means "any stage" on that side, so a
bare trigger fires on every lifecycle transition.

from_stage.description:
Optional canonical origin-stage filter. Omit or send null to match
any origin stage.

to_stage.description:
Optional canonical destination-stage filter. Omit or send null to
match any destination stage.

SUB-013 catalog-linked profile attributes, computed from commerce
events and stored on subscriber_computed_traits under the
well-known keys favorite_category + last_viewed_sku. Read via
GET /api/v1/subscribers/{id}/catalog-attributes.

null when the subscriber has no catalog history yet.

ChannelConsent.description:
SUB-042 — one (profile, channel) consent row. A profile may carry up to
five rows (email / sms / push / whatsapp / rcs), each with its own
status, consent timestamp/source, and a shared frequency cap. The
denormalised email/phone_e164 mirror the canonical subscriber row for
send-time join efficiency. Listed via
GET /api/v1/subscribers/{id}/channel-consents and upserted via
PATCH /api/v1/subscribers/{id}/channel-consents/{channel}.

channel.description: The reachability channel this consent row governs.

consent_source.description: Reviewed source label for the current decision; unknown means no defensible source is recorded.

consent_timestamp.description: When the current status was recorded. Re-stamped on status change unless supplied explicitly.

email.description: Denormalised canonical email for send-time joins. May be empty.

frequency_cap_until.description: Shared frequency cap — sends to this channel are held until this passes. null = no active cap.

subscriber_version.description: Fresh strong parent-subscriber revision returned by PATCH and repeated in its ETag header. Omitted from list rows.

ChannelSendTime.description:
SUB-066 — per-channel optimal send window for one (subscriber,
channel) pair (subscriber_channel_consents, migration 0936).
best_send_hour is a modal hour-of-week 0-167 (UTC-bucketed); null
when no per-channel value has been computed. day_of_week (0=Sunday)
and hour_of_day are derived for UI convenience.

best_send_hour.description: Modal hour-of-week 0-167 (UTC). null = not computed; fall back to the aggregate.

best_send_hour_at.description: When best_send_hour was last computed for this channel.

Rates are conversion percentages (0..100) relative to the prior stage.
Purchase counts include only currently paid orders from subscriber
signup through the query snapshot. They are lifetime-to-date, so cohort
age affects maturity.

Conversion.description:
One append-only tenant conversion fact. Recipient email and arbitrary
properties may contain personal or tenant-sensitive data and must not
be logged or exposed outside the owning tenant.

amount_cents.description: Optional caller-supplied amount in the smallest currency unit. Signed values allow refunds and adjustments; current ingestion restricts them to JavaScript's safe-integer range.

attributed_via.description:
Honest provenance for current rows; historical unclassified rows
can omit this field:

- `explicit`: a tenant-owned campaign hint asserted by the caller.
- `last_touch`: heuristic match to the recipient's recent email click.
- `none`: no tenant-owned campaign could be attributed.
- `code_redemption`: outcome linked through one campaign assignment;
  not proof of who redeemed the code or read the message.
- `campaign_vanity_path`: outcome linked through a shared campaign
  path; campaign scope only.

campaign_id.description: Present only when attribution resolved to a tenant-owned campaign. It may reflect an explicit caller assertion or heuristic last-touch; consult attributed_via rather than treating it as certain causal attribution.

currency.description: Uppercase three-letter ASCII currency code required exactly when amount_cents is present. Syntax is enforced but membership in an ISO currency allowlist is not.

event_name.description: Trimmed tenant-defined name. Current ingestion rejects Unicode controls and counts this limit in Unicode code points.

properties.description: Arbitrary caller-defined JSON properties. Treat the entire object as tenant-sensitive and potentially recipient-identifying.

subscriber_email.description: Optional normalized caller-supplied recipient identifier. Current ingestion validates one exact address but does not verify ownership or mailbox control.

campaign_id.description:
Tenant campaign UUID, or an empty string on the final synthetic
`(other campaigns)` rollup row.

revenue_cents.description: Revenue in the response's dominant currency only.

campaign_vanity_path.description: Outcomes linked through a shared campaign path; campaign-scope evidence only.

code_redemption.description: Outcomes linked through one issued-code assignment; not proof of redeemer or reader identity.

last_touch.description: Heuristic seven-day click attribution; not proof of causality.

unclassified.description: Legacy rows not yet processed by the bounded backfill.

currency.description: Omitted when the scoped window has no monetary conversions.
Omitted when the window has no monetary conversions.

total_revenue_cents.description: Attributed plus unattributed revenue in the dominant currency.

ConversionEmailHMACProjectionErrorCode.description:

`identity_projection_status` is `failed`; arbitrary worker, database,
KMS, address, digest, and secret detail is never exposed.

Closed readiness state for the indexed email-HMAC identity projection
belonging to this exact signing key. Only `ready` permits requests
containing `email_hmac_sha256`; `pending` and `failed` fail closed.

next_cursor.description: Omitted on the terminal page; pass unchanged as the next request's cursor.

identity_projection_updated_at.description:

This is the timestamp of the current public projection state.

key_id.description: Globally unique non-secret identifier used in the v2 signature preimage.

revoked_at.description: Present when the key is permanently revoked.

message.const: Content-Type must be application/json.

CreateAuditAccessRequestInput.description:
The body is optional. Repeating the call while a request is pending is
idempotent and does NOT overwrite the original note or creation time,
so a second note is silently ignored rather than applied. A supplied
note is trimmed and must not exceed 1,000 UTF-8 bytes.

content_revision_id.description: Optional exact immutable revision. If omitted, the server freezes the current draft.

include_seed_test.description:
Requests controlled observation from named seed environments. The
current runtime returns `controlled_observation_unavailable`
before creating a snapshot/run because no adapter is configured.

observed_surfaces.description:
Optional stable adapter surface identifiers. Valid only when
include_seed_test is true; identifiers do not imply availability.

request_id.description: Stable UUID for this logical immutable-run request.

send_plan_id.description: Optional already-ready plan; requires content_revision_id. If omitted, the server owns compilation and materialization.

content_blocks.description: Semantic-email v2 nodes when source_mode=semantic; otherwise the historical block payload. Unknown semantic node fields are rejected.

list_id.description: Send to one list: its numeric id (the `id` the lists catalogue returns) or the list's uuid (`postwave_uuid` on list responses). The list is resolved within the workspace and stored by numeric id; one this workspace does not have is refused with 422 list_not_found. A campaign targets one list or one segment, not both (422 ambiguous_audience); with neither it sends to every eligible contact in the workspace.

CreateFederationLinkInput.description: SUB-023 POST body. parent_tenant_id must be this workspace's agency parent.

token.description:
The one-time invite token, returned exactly once. Compose the
accept link as /accept-invite?token=<token>. Only its SHA-256 is
stored server-side.

CreateLookalikeInput.description:
SUB-033 lookalike-audience generation request. The audience is built by
ranking non-seed subscribers by first-party similarity to the seed
segment's members.

confidence_threshold.description:
Optional similarity floor in [0.5,1]; candidates below it are dropped.
null/omitted = no floor (take the top `size`).

data_use_acknowledged.description: Explicit acknowledgement of the first-party modeling data-use notice.

name.description: Optional display name for the generated audience.

seed_segment_id.description: The segment whose members define the lookalike seed.

size.description: Target audience size; the ranker returns up to this many members.

CreateSubscriberInput.description:
Subscriber upsert payload. `status` defaults to `unconfirmed` and
`consent_source` to `unknown`. If status is `enabled`, the caller must
provide consent_timestamp, a single/double opt-in consent_source,
consent_channel, consent_legal_basis, consent_evidence,
consent_reason, consent_policy_version, and a two-letter country.
Consent fields are rejected on non-sendable statuses; use the consent
ledger endpoints for historical non-sendable decisions.

CreateSubscriberNoteInput.description:
SUB-097 POST body for /api/v1/subscribers/{id}/notes. Supply
markdown_body (preferred) or the legacy plain body; at least one must
be non-empty. markdown_body may embed @[Name](user:id) mention tokens.

detail.description: May contain a clicked URL, SMS body, or consent proof text.

dns_records.description:
Persisted DNS challenges and their latest observations. Current
registration emits exactly one CNAME and one TXT record; reads
reject corrupted stored rows containing more than 16 records.

tenantId.description: Authenticated tenant that owns the row.

verified.description:
True only when every persisted DNS challenge matched during the
latest explicit verification. This is not TLS, edge-routing, or
serving-readiness evidence and may regress on a later check.

verifiedAt.description:
Nullable RFC 3339 timestamp corresponding to storage
`verified_at`. It records the latest successful check and is
cleared when a later check fails. The current Go encoder omits the
camelCase `verifiedAt` wire property when the value is nil; the
desktop decoder also accepts an explicit null for compatibility.

error.message: that domain is already registered

domain.description:
Requested hostname. The handler trims surrounding whitespace,
lowercases valid ASCII input, and stores the canonical result.

Record owner name. New registrations cap the complete owner at
253 characters. The 270-character compatibility ceiling keeps

value.description: Required CNAME target or exact TXT ownership token.

verified.description: Whether this individual record matched on the latest check.

CustomDomainDNSVerificationError.description: Safe fixed reason from the most recent DNS check.

CustomDomainHostname.description:
Canonical lowercase ASCII hostname with at least two labels. Each
label is at most 63 characters and cannot start or end with a hyphen.
IP addresses, all-numeric ambiguous IPv4 forms, wildcards, empty
labels, Unicode, IDNA `xn--` labels, ports, schemes, paths, localhost,
and other single-label/private names are rejected. This wider response
schema keeps historical rows up to DNS's 253-character hostname limit
readable; new registrations use the narrower challenge-safe schema.

CustomDomainID.description:
Lowercase UUID emitted by the custom-domain repository. The desktop
decoder has a broader safe-identifier compatibility ceiling of 128
characters, but current API-created identifiers are UUIDs.

CustomDomainListResponse.description:
Unpaginated, newest-first custom-domain rows. The server currently has
no list bound; the first-party desktop decoder deliberately rejects
arrays over 500 items, so tenants approaching that compatibility limit
require a pagination/server-bound follow-up before additional growth.

Intended hostname surface: hosted signup forms, link/redirect traffic,
hosted web/archive content, or branded open-pixel tracking. Sending
identities use the separate sending-identities contract.

CustomDomainRegistrationHostname.description:
Raw new-registration hostname input. Surrounding ASCII whitespace and
hostname letter case are accepted; the handler trims and lowercases
before persistence. The normalized 236-character ceiling reserves 17

`_postwave-verify.` so the issued TXT owner never exceeds DNS's
253-character textual hostname ceiling. The raw-string maxLength is a
coarse reflection of the endpoint's stricter 32 KiB total-body limit.

config.description: Type-specific metadata (SUB-006). Absent for plain scalar fields.

Type-specific metadata for a custom field (SUB-006). All members are

declared type. Null/absent for plain scalar fields.

data_classification.description:
SUB-057 schema-level data label. The richer successor to pii_flag:
the policy engine reads it to enforce masking, retention, export,
and consent-filtering rules. Absent or "none" means unclassified.

pii_flag.description: Marks the field as personally-identifiable information.

schema.description: Property-name → scalar FieldType map for an object field.

Rejected with 422 if the tenant is already at its
max_searchable_fields cap.

Resolved custom-field governance state for a tenant (SUB-015): the
effective soft-limit caps plus live usage counts. Effective limits are

Patch for a custom field's mutable metadata (SUB-006). key + type are

CustomObjectProperties.description: Bounded record data capped at 768 KiB, depth 32, 20,000 nodes, and 1,024 entries per container.

expectedVersion.description: Zero creates only; a positive value must equal the loaded record version.

CustomObjectSchema.description:
Bounded Moosewave JSON-Schema subset. The optional root type must be
`object`; supported nested types are object, string, number, integer,
boolean, and array. Supported constraints are properties, required,
items, enum, minLength, maxLength, minimum, maximum, and
additionalProperties. Schema documents are capped at 256 KiB, depth
20, 4,096 nodes, 1,024 entries per container, and 256 declared fields.

detail.description: Human-readable review note. Required when `evidence` is omitted.

evidence.description: Operator-held evidence references. Required when `detail` is omitted.

key.description: Allow-listed migration evidence key. ActiveCampaign keys cover consent/exclusion, deliverability, automation rebuild, audience/schema/campaign/content/CRM gaps, and cleanup authorization. Beehiiv keys cover consent, dynamic rules, archive fidelity, automation retirement, website, network, and ad review. HubSpot uses `hubspot_crm_bridge_scope_review` for the post-final-snapshot scope checklist and `hubspot_post_pilot_cleanup` for strict-pilot-bound local-session/rollback/token-cleanup authorization. Klaviyo keys cover profile identity/consent, frozen audiences, flows, channels, deliverability, and ecosystem dependencies. Customer.io keys cover global plus channel/topic consent and ESP suppression, immutable cio_id/duplicate-email identity and frozen audiences, automation rebuild/retirement, non-email/transactional dependencies, deliverability, and ecosystem dependencies. Shared keys cover source warnings and SMS readiness. Passing evidence is bound to the latest final delta/full snapshot.

status.description: Defaults to `pass`; passing evidence is accepted only after the final delta import completes.

fanout_enabled.description: When true, collect read-only matching records from connected stores. Provider deletion policy is never executed.
Connected-store erasure is not implemented; this must be false.

external_stores_affected.description: Provider erasure is not implemented by this endpoint.

placeholder.description: Non-deliverable synthetic identity retained for referential integrity.

rows_deleted.description: Total Moosewave-managed records anonymized, deleted, inserted, or updated by the erasure transaction.

DSARStoreResponse.description:
SUB-053 — one per-store read-only access receipt. Produced when a
Subject Access Request is created with fanout_enabled=true: the
orchestrator enumerates connected commerce stores and searches each for
the subject by email. Provider auto-delete policy is ignored and no
destructive adapter method is called. Read via
GET /api/v1/sar/requests/{id}/store-responses (admin scope).

customer_id.description: The provider-side customer id matched for the subject (empty when not found).

receipt_url.description: Compliance receipt URL proving the deletion/retention decision.

response.description: Raw provider response (or {error} on failure) for the audit trail.

surface.description: OVR-032 — which dashboard this layout belongs to.

emails_sent.description: Legacy gross sent-event volume; not a dashboard rate denominator.

unique_clicks.description: Distinct campaign-recipient click pairs in the comparison window.

unique_opens.description: Distinct campaign-recipient open pairs in the comparison window.

last_updated.description: Omitted when the tenant has never completed a predictive recompute.

subscriber matched a segment or was included in a campaign.

SUB-021 per-workspace deduplication settings. The auto-merge confidence
threshold is the client's initial review filter. Complete server scan

Initial confidence (0..1) used by duplicate-review clients.

mfa_code.description: Required when the user has a confirmed TOTP enrollment.

DeliverabilityDmarcAggregateReportID.description: Tenant-scoped UUID of an ingested aggregate report.

DeliverabilityDmarcCount.description: Nonnegative aggregate count bounded to JavaScript's exact integer range.

DeliverabilityDmarcDisposition.description: Receiver-reported DMARC disposition, not final-delivery or inbox-placement evidence.

`none`; this is not final-delivery or inbox-placement evidence.

unknown.description: Messages with a missing or unrecognized receiver disposition.

DeliverabilityDmarcDomainScope.description: Empty string denotes all report domains in the authenticated tenant.

Canonical lowercase ASCII policy domain. Labels are one to 63
characters and cannot begin or end with a hyphen. Empty labels,
trailing dots, IP addresses, whitespace, Unicode, ports, schemes, and

latestReportAt.description: Newest ingestion timestamp in scope; omitted when there are no reports.

reportingDays.description: Number of returned positive-message daily series points.

sourceListTruncated.description: True exactly when more than ten source IPs are in scope.

topFailingSources.description:
Up to ten sources with at least 20 messages and less than 80%
alignment, ordered by estimated unaligned message volume.

topSources.description: Up to ten source IPs ordered by observed message volume descending.

Normalized `p=` value observed in an aggregate report. Empty denotes a

availableDomains.description: Alphabetical, tenant-wide domain inventory independent of the active list filter.

domainInventoryTruncated.description: True when more than 500 distinct tenant report domains exist.

envelopeFromDomain.description: Canonical hostname extracted from one dominant envelope-from observation. Mailbox local-parts and arbitrary raw identifiers are withheld; omitted when no safe hostname can be derived.

perReport.description: Newest-first bounded evidence rows with aggregate-report UUID tie-breaking.

note.description:

interoperable code-point ceiling and the vendor extension records

notes.description: Reviewer notes copied into the marketplace audit trail.

DeviceGrantAccount.description: Authenticated approver identity shown only on the consent endpoint.

DeviceGrantCancelResponse.description:
Idempotent cancellation result. If this capability had already created
a session, cancellation also revokes that exact bound session.

DeviceGrantDecisionRequest.description:
Session-grant mutations must follow an inspect call and echo its
memory-held `consent_token`. The token is optional for legacy API-key
approvals. An omitted action remains the legacy API-key approve form.

action.description: Omission is the backwards-compatible API-key approval behavior.

consent_token.description:
Opaque proof returned by inspecting this session grant. Keep it in
memory and echo it unchanged on approve or deny; never log it.

user_code.description: Eight-character code; separators and case are normalized by the server.

consent_token.description:
Present only when inspecting a session grant. Opaque, short-lived,
and bound to the reviewed grant, tenant, user, and approving
session; keep it in memory and never render or persist it.

ok.description: True for completed approve/deny mutations; absent for read-only inspect.

requires_mfa.description: The approving account must complete its policy-required MFA step-up before mutation.

scopes.description: Role-derived scopes for API-key grants only.

DeviceGrantKind.description: The credential produced by a device grant.

DeviceGrantSessionConfirmationSuccess.description:
Successful idempotent acknowledgement of the exact provisional
session. The Set-Cookie value is now active for the returned
tenant-capped lifetime. Retrying with the same device capability and
exact cookie returns this same session rather than creating another.

expires_in.description: Remaining activated session lifetime in seconds, after the tenant cap.

DeviceGrantSessionSuccess.description:
Successful session poll or recovery replay. When
`confirmation_required` is true, the Set-Cookie value is provisional
and cannot authenticate normal endpoints; immediately confirm it using
the same device code. A false value can occur when replaying the exact
already-confirmed cookie after a lost poll response. Replays never mint
another session.

confirmation_expires_in.description: Seconds remaining in the narrow confirmation/replay recovery window.

confirmation_required.description: True until the exact provisional cookie has been acknowledged by `action: confirm`.

expires_in.description:
Intended tenant-capped session lifetime while provisional; actual
remaining activated lifetime on an already-confirmed replay.

DeviceGrantStartRequest.description: Unknown legacy CLI fields are ignored for backwards compatibility.

remember.description:

A missing or empty layout uses the exact non-empty source body with a warning; a non-empty layout must contain exactly one documented `{{content}}` slot. `A` is an external ZeroBounce/Kickbox-valid address checked within 30

or accepted delivery. `C` is external ZeroBounce/Kickbox catch-all. `D` has a historical hard bounce,
soft bounce, or ambiguous negative within 30 days that a newer trusted
positive has not retired. `F` has a provider-invalid, spam-trap, abuse,
or do-not-mail verdict; a complaint; or an authoritative consent or
active-suppression hard stop. `U` has no decisive fresh evidence. An
active soft-bounce suppression can retain grade `D` while its
recommendation is `blocked`.

{hash}@{domain} label safe to display, and email_hash is the SHA-256
hex of the (now-erased) lowercased address that a downstream DSAR tool
recomputes to match the receipt. Fetched via
GET /api/v1/subscribers/{id}/erasure-receipt (admin scope).

gateway clamps this to the caller's own cursor, which is 0 for every
time-mode request, and a client folding that in would resume from
`sequence_id > 0` -- the oldest page of the whole retained log -- on
every reconnect from then on.

The TIME cursor a streaming client resumes from, or empty when the
caller paginates by sequence and the page scanned nothing. Live SSE
payloads carry `at` but never a sequence id, so this is the only
cursor a dropped connection can resume from.

NotificationChannelDelivery.description:
One channel's record of one notification. The four channels keep
separate ledgers with different status vocabularies, so `status` is the
channel's own word and `outcome` is the normalized cross-channel answer.

notification_id.description:
The notification_feed row this mirrors — the identity every channel
carries. Absent when a ledger row has no linkable notification.

outcome.description:
Normalized across channels. `accepted` means a provider took the
message; only `delivered` means arrival was confirmed.

reason.description:
Why it was suppressed or how it failed — `quiet_hours`,
`preference_in_app_off`, `DeviceNotRegistered`, a provider status
phrase. Absent on success. URLs are redacted to their host because a
webhook destination path can itself be a credential.

target.description:
Distinguishes two records of the same channel without exposing a
credential: a digest of the push endpoint, the device id, or the
webhook payload kind. Never the endpoint or destination URL.

NotificationPreferences.description:
A user's notification preferences as a category × channel matrix. Each
`*_on_<category>` flag governs one channel for one category. In-app
defaults on (it preserves the pre-split delivery behavior); the webhook
channel defaults off and only fires when a `notification_webhook_url` is
also set.

notification_webhook_kind.description: Payload flavor for the webhook channel. Both send a Slack-compatible text body.

notification_webhook_url.description: Outbound webhook destination for the webhook channel; empty when unset.

usage_alert_threshold_pct.description: Percent of plan usage that triggers a usage alert (0 disables).

NotificationPreferencesPatch.description:
Partial update of a user's notification preferences. Every field is
optional; an omitted field preserves the stored value. Booleans toggle a
single channel for a single category.

notification_webhook_url.description: Empty string clears the destination; a value sets it (validated as an https public host).

usage_alert_threshold_pct.description: 0 disables usage alerts; 1..100 sets the threshold.

Offer.description: One canonical offer, addressable by a URL that outlives the campaign that promoted it.

inventory_state.description: `unknown` is a real member. Defaulting a missing inventory feed to `in_stock` would have an agent act on availability nobody asserted.

price_cents.description: Minor units. Always accompanied by currency — the schema enforces the pairing, because a price with no currency is not a price.

valid_until.description: In the body, not only in a cache header: a header tells a cache when to re-ask, this tells a reasoner when the answer stopped being true.

actionable.description: True only when validity, inventory, and a safe HTTPS action target all permit action.

reason.description: Optional personal rationale stored with this decision.
Optional personal rationale; an empty string clears an existing reason.

step_key.description: Nonblank onboarding step key after trimming.

steps.description: step_key to decision; an absent key has no recorded decision.

List-Unsubscribe.description: Canonical RFC 8058 form value. The runtime comparison is case-insensitive for mailbox-provider compatibility.

OpaqueSubscriberIdentifier.description: Stable opaque subscriber identifier. Email addresses and other PII are not accepted.

OrderCadenceMetrics.description:
SUB-062 compact repeat-purchase projection hydrated inline on the
subscriber detail GET. Read from the same average_days_between_orders
computed trait the SUB-061 replenishment-cadence worker maintains. A
null projection (omitted from the Subscriber) means the profile has no
computed cadence yet (no, or a single, order).

average_days_between_orders.description: Rolling mean number of days between consecutive orders.

last_computed_at.description: When the cadence worker last refreshed the metric.

failed.description: Exhausted plus pending rows with a recorded error.

skipped.description: Work cancelled by permanent endpoint deletion.

auth_config_status.description: Delivery is paused unless receiver authentication is ready or absent. Replace or clear pending/invalid credentials.

config_version.description: Monotonic revision of delivery-relevant configuration. Confirm this value in expected_webhook_config_version immediately before a live playground fire.

delivery_policy_status.description: Invalid policies remain readable for repair but are never executed.

filter_expression.description: Optional bounded non-executable filter DSL (maximum 4096 UTF-8 bytes and 32 conditions), applied to the canonical envelope.

list_id.description: Optional list scope for list.subscriber.* events only. The list is durably constrained to the same tenant.

url.description: Safe display projection such as `https://host/…?…`; never the complete receiver path or query and never valid PATCH input.

url_status.description: Readiness of the envelope-backed complete destination.

filter_expression.description: Bounded filter DSL; invalid syntax returns `400 invalid_filter`.

list_id.description: Must identify a list owned by the active workspace.

public_key_pem.description: Asymmetric public verification key; private material is never returned.

OutboundWebhookEnvelope.description: Canonical body before an optional customer transform. Delivery headers are X-Postwave-Signature, X-Postwave-Event, X-Postwave-Event-Id, X-Postwave-Delivery, optional X-Postwave-Key-Id, and X-Postwave-Test=true for probes. event.id is stable across retries/replays; delivery.id identifies one lineage row.

id.description: Unique attempt lineage row; changes on manual replay.
Stable across retries and manual replay.

deliveries_skipped.description: Deletion-cancelled rows; excluded from failure and top-error aggregates.

expected_webhook_config_version.description: Exact monotonic configuration version selected and confirmed by the operator. The live request is rejected if any delivery-relevant webhook configuration changed before fire.

fire_id.description: Caller-minted durable identity for this one logical fire. Retain it through cancellation. A missing receipt never proves the original request cannot still arrive, so continue only with this same ID and its exact original Idempotency-Key; never mint a replacement merely because reconciliation currently returns 404.

payload.description: Optional event.data object. Omission uses the catalog sample for event_type; explicit null is invalid. Canonical JSON is limited to 262,144 UTF-8 bytes, depth 24, 20,000 nodes, 2,000 fields per object, 256-byte keys, and 131,072-byte strings. Duplicate object members are rejected recursively and JSON numbers retain their exact decimal representation. The whole request is limited to 524,288 bytes. Use synthetic data only: the request inspection and bounded receiver response are envelope-encrypted and retained under the tenant's webhook-delivery retention policy before cryptoshred; payload-free side-effect identity digests remain to prevent replay.

OutboundWebhookPlaygroundFireOutcome.description: `filtered` proves no receiver contact; `receiver_responded` proves an HTTP response was received regardless of its status; and `transport_ambiguous` means the receiver may have processed the request even though Moosewave received no HTTP response.

completed_at.description: Null only while state is pending.

event_type.description: Event type frozen when the fire was reserved. Historical values remain readable even after removal from the current fire catalog.

outcome.description: Empty only while state is pending.

ambiguous.description: True only when receiver execution cannot be determined.

body.description: Exact post-filter/transform request body with credential redaction.

error.description: Bounded, credential-redacted transport or receiver error.

event_id.description: Stable event identity derived from fire_id.

filtered.description: True when policy prevented the live receiver request.

headers.description: Exact safe request headers. Receiver-auth values are replaced with [REDACTED].

response_body.description: Bounded, credential-redacted receiver response preview. Empty when the upstream body exceeded the safe preview limit.

response_body_truncated.description: True when the receiver body exceeded 4 KiB or could not be read completely; the unsafe partial preview is withheld.

signature.description: X-Postwave-Signature value; empty only when filtered.

status_code.description: Zero for transport ambiguity; 204 when filtered.

OutboundWebhookReceiverAuthMetadata.description: Value-free receiver-auth metadata. This schema deliberately has no bearer token, custom-header values, certificate, or private key.

OutboundWebhookReceiverAuthWrite.description: Receiver credentials accepted only on create/update and envelope-encrypted at rest. Credential values are never returned.

OutboundWebhookTestResult.description: Synchronous result of the canonical webhook.test probe. Receiver credentials are redacted from response and error previews.

filtered.description: True when the configured filter suppressed the probe.

key_ids.description: Fingerprints corresponding to the signing material.

redaction_applied.description: True when credential-like response text was redacted.

signature.description: Request-bound Moosewave signature; empty when filtered.

status_code.description: Receiver status, or zero when no HTTP response was received.

OutboundWebhookTransformTemplate.description: Maps at most 64 nonempty output field names to RFC 6901 JSON Pointers. Each pointer is at most 1024 UTF-8 bytes and 32 path segments; an empty pointer selects the entire canonical envelope. The encoded template is limited to 16384 bytes.

OutboundWebhookUpdateInput.description: Partial update. Omit auth_config to preserve credentials, send null or type=none to clear them, or send a full credential object to replace them atomically. Omit url to preserve the encrypted destination and never round-trip the redacted read projection. Omit filter/transform to preserve or send null to clear.

url.description: Complete replacement URL. Projections containing `…` are rejected with `redacted_destination`.

PIIFinding.description:
SUB-071 — one shadow-PII detection: undeclared PII found in a subscriber
free-text field and queued for DPO review. New evidence is a
tenant-separated, domain-separated HMAC-SHA256 fingerprint. Historical
bare hashes were destroyed and replaced with random legacy-redacted
linkage tokens; neither representation contains the matched cleartext.

oneOf.description: An unreviewed queue item has no reviewer stamp or receipt.
A terminal item always carries its immutable review receipt.

field_name.description: The custom/merge field key the suspect value lived under.

fingerprint.description: Lowercase 64-hex keyed fingerprint, or a random non-recomputable legacy-redacted linkage token.

reviewed_by.description: Stable non-PII actor reference. User/API-key actor IDs are canonical UUIDs; migrated legacy labels were discarded and replaced by random non-recomputable tokens.

comment.description: Required reviewer rationale. Raw personal data is rejected; cite evidence_reference instead.

reason.description: Must belong to the selected status's outcome-specific reason set; legacy_migrated is never accepted.

PIIFindingReviewReceipt.description: Immutable one-to-one DPO decision receipt. Its fingerprint and provenance exactly equal the finding snapshot and never contain detected cleartext.

actor_id.description: Canonical user/API-key UUID, or a random non-recomputable 64-hex migration token when actor_type is legacy.

finding_updated_at.description: The pre-review finding version matched by expected_updated_at.

reason.description: Outcome-specific decision reason. legacy_migrated is response-only for pre-1760 terminal rows whose original rationale was unavailable.

PIIScanConfig.description:
SUB-071 per-tenant scanner config and truthful runtime capability/version
disclosure. `scan_enabled` is an opt-in; only `enabled_caught_up` together
with an exact evidence snapshot and zero known gaps supports a bounded
current `subscribers`-row projection coverage claim. Retained attribute
history, notes/attachments, and event/content payload stores are not
covered. Intermediate revisions may be explicitly coalesced, while
truncation and exhausted retries remain visible gaps.

oneOf.description: Scanner dependencies are unavailable; scan_enabled preserves the tenant opt-in while execution remains unavailable.
Scanner dependencies exist, but tenant opt-in is disabled.
Tenant opt-in is enabled; status/evidence disclose backfill, exact catch-up, or known gaps.

scan_schedule.description: Present only while clearing historical inert state; scheduled scans are unavailable.

snapshot_exact.description: False means counters are progress telemetry. True means the reconciler serialized the current subscribers-row projection count against all scan-relevant writers for that projection; it does not certify retained history, notes/attachments, or event/content payload stores.

limit.description: Bounded dead-letter batch; zero or omitted uses 50. Ignored for reconciliation.

routing_key.description: PagerDuty Events API routing key; only its minimum shape is checked.

Passkey.description: A stored WebAuthn credential (passkey) for the authenticated user.

backed_up.description: True when the authenticator syncs this passkey (multi-device).

name.description: Trimmed safe display text; the runtime ceiling is UTF-8 bytes.

PerChannelSendTimes.description:
SUB-066 response for GET /api/v1/subscribers/{id}/send-times. The
per-channel windows (channels) alongside the legacy per-subscriber
aggregate (subscribers.best_send_hour, migration 0076). Callers
prefer a channel's best_send_hour and fall back to
aggregate_best_send_hour when it is null.

PhonePreview.description: One phone field's before/after within a transform preview.

PoweredIncrementalLift.description: Immutable final F02 result emitted only after the configured power gate passes. Underpowered or unavailable results are omitted entirely; their point estimates must not surface through F12.

methodology_statement.description: Self-contained explanation of the F02 population, outcome, statistical method, power gate, and suppression rule.

relative_lift.description: Percentage lift, not a ratio (10% to 15% is 50); omitted when the control rate is zero and relative lift is undefined.

window_end.description: Exclusive caller-fixed analysis bound; not an assertion that campaign sending completed at this time.

window_start.description: Inclusive caller-fixed analysis bound; not an assertion of the campaign's first send time.

PreSendExcludedSubscriber.description: SUB-067 one churn-risk-suppressed subscriber in the preview sample.

PreSendRefineInput.description:
SUB-067 pre-send audience refine request. All fields optional; zero
values use the defaults (churn_threshold=80, cooling_off_hours=24).

churn_threshold.description: Exclude subscribers with churn_score at/above this (default 80).

cooling_off_hours.description: Auto re-entry window in hours (default 24; 0 = no auto re-entry).

dry_run.description: Preview counts + sample without persisting exclusion rows.

exclude_recently_paused.description: Also drop subscribers already holding an unexpired exclusion on another campaign.

PreSendRefineResult.description:
SUB-067 response for POST/GET /api/v1/campaigns/{id}/presend-refine: the
excluded count, cooling-off count + window, and a bounded sample.

error.description: Stable public error text; raw downstream details are never returned.

score.description:
Present for completed checks, including a real zero. EQ and voice
use 0..100; placement uses 0..1. Omitted for error/skipped checks.

PreSendVerdictInput.description:
Current editor content. Fields are optional at the JSON-shape layer so
the EQ component can return an actionable critical score for an empty
or incomplete draft instead of rejecting it before evaluation. Sender
authentication and reputation are resolved from authenticated
tenant-scoped server records, never from caller-supplied claims.

campaign_id.description:
Requests the fourth Campaign Assurance component. Supplying only
this field honestly returns not_assured when no exact frozen run is
available; content_revision_id and source_hash must otherwise be
supplied together with it.

campaign_assurance.description: Exact frozen-snapshot identity and gate disposition; omitted when Campaign Assurance was not requested.

complete.description:
True only when all three base components and, when requested, the
exact Campaign Assurance component completed successfully.

verdict.description: Priority is critical, then incomplete, then warn, then ok.

Per-feature explainability snapshot (top features / weights / raw

SUB-010 upsert body for the predictive metadata snapshot. score_type
defaults to "churn" when omitted. At least one of model_version,
confidence or features is required.

confidence.description: Model confidence in [0,1]; null = below the minimum-data threshold.

Per-feature explainability snapshot. When supplied (non-null) it
replaces the stored snapshot; omitted leaves any existing snapshot
untouched.

model_version.description: Freeform model version stamped by the scorer.

score_type.description: Which cached predictive scalar to attach metadata to (default "churn").

PredictionMetadataList.description:
SUB-010 response for GET/PATCH /api/v1/subscribers/{id}/prediction-metadata:
every per-score-type metadata snapshot for one subscriber.

PreviewTransformInput.description:
SUB-018 dry-run request. Applies the tenant's transforms (or the inline
overrides) to a sample identifier without persisting anything.

Preview an as-yet-unsaved config instead of the stored one. Omit to
use the tenant's saved config.

affected_subject_count.description:
An explicit zero is preserved. Absence means no count was recorded;
it must not be inferred as a measured zero.

gdpr_72h_deadline.description: System operational clock; not proof that a statutory deadline applies.

notification_decisions.description: Operator/system metadata; not independently verified legal or delivery evidence.

incident_id.description: Parent incident identity for cross-binding this ledger response.

PrivacyIncidentJurisdictionReference.description:
Safe data-capture metadata only. Presence in this catalog means the
code is recognized by the product; it does not assert legal coverage,
an applicable duty, a deadline, a recipient, or current legal advice.

An explicit release hold returned instead of an obligation-shaped
jurisdiction result. It identifies only which submitted codes the
product recognizes. The disjoint union of `recognized[].code` and
`unknown_jurisdictions` is the normalized jurisdiction-code set on the
same incident row. It makes no authoritative legal determination.

nextCursor.description: Opaque keyset cursor; omitted on the terminal page.

body_sha256.description: Legacy caller-supplied value; not a verified response digest or signature.

recipient_ref.description: Legacy operator-authored reference; not a provider delivery receipt.

State reviewed by the operator. A mismatch with the current locked

totalDistinctEventNames.description: Distinct names in the complete period before the top-200 limit.

items.description: Raw events ordered by occurredAt descending.

asOf.description: Server-captured upper bound shared by every aggregate.

daily.description: Exactly periodDays consecutive UTC date buckets ordered oldest first, with zero-count buckets retained.

email.description: Canonical subscriber email used when subscriber_id is omitted.

Per-subscriber predictive analytics: CLV prediction joined with the
RFM score. Backs the per-subscriber RFM profile card (SUB-126) and
the predictive profile list.

ProfileObjectLink.description:
Binding of a custom object record to a subscriber profile (SUB-011),
backed by profile_object_links. The listing variant hydrates the
denormalized type (key/label) + record (externalId/properties) so
the profile UI renders without a second round-trip.

name.description: Tenant-unique rule name; posting the same name replaces the rule.

source_path.description: Merge/custom-field key, or a dotted path for json_path transforms.

target_key.description: Key written into the subscriber's custom_fields object.

policy_version.description: Compatibility hint ignored for evidence; the server selects the policy version from the resolved site key.

proof_text.description: Reserved server-authenticated field. Public requests must omit it or send an empty value; non-empty values return 422.

site_key.description: Compatibility public site-key transport used only when the preferred header and query forms are absent.

subject_email.description: Reserved server-authenticated field. Public requests must omit it or send an empty value; non-empty values return 422.

tenant_id.description: Optional workspace assertion. When supplied it must exactly match the workspace resolved from the public site key.

visitor_id.description: Pseudonymous first-party browser identity; never an email address or dashboard principal.

PublicConsentPreferences.description:
Browser preference projection. Every supplied essential, analytics, or
marketing value must be a JSON boolean; supplied `essential` must be
true and is always recorded true. Without a Sec-GPC header, `accept`
requires analytics=true and marketing=true, `reject` and `gpc` require
both false or omitted, and `custom` permits a mixed pair. Sec-GPC: 1
overrides a racing valid accept/custom body and forces both false.
Additional preference keys are accepted for forward compatibility but
do not change the v1 decision fingerprint.

decision_id.description: Durable identity shared by exactly the three event rows for this browser decision.

idempotency_key.description: Exact echo of the validated Idempotency-Key. Present on every keyed first-write and replay; omitted only for deprecated keyless writes. Clients must match it to the pending request before acknowledging delivery.

idempotent.description: True for keyed first-writes and replays; false only for a deprecated keyless write.

written.description: Logical batch size. A keyed replay still returns 3 because it reconstructs the original response.

message.const: Request body is not valid JSON.

PublicConversionInput.description:
Public, untrusted conversion payload. Unknown properties are ignored by
the current runtime. All values are assertions by the caller; neither
subscriber identity nor revenue integrity is verified.

amount_cents.description: Optional signed amount in the smallest currency unit, bounded to JavaScript's safe-integer range. Supplying it requires currency.

campaign_id.description: Optional untrusted campaign hint. Invalid, stale, or foreign-tenant values degrade to an unattributed conversion instead of failing.

currency.description: Required when amount_cents is present and otherwise omitted or blank. It is trimmed, uppercased, and must contain exactly three ASCII letters when used; no ISO membership allowlist is enforced.

email.description: Optional value trimmed and validated as one exact address of at most 320 UTF-8 bytes. Identity and mailbox control remain unverified.

event_name.description: Trimmed tenant-defined name with no Unicode controls. Omitted or whitespace-only values become conversion.

properties.description: Optional arbitrary JSON metadata stored with the conversion.

message.const: too many requests

enum: event_name must be 1 to 128 characters after trimming and contain no control characters
email must be a single exact address of at most 320 bytes
currency must be exactly 3 ASCII letters when amount_cents is present
currency must be omitted when amount_cents is omitted
amount_cents must be a JavaScript-safe integer between -9007199254740991 and 9007199254740991

message.const: unauthorized

PublicOffer.description: Allowlisted unauthenticated projection of one canonical offer. Arbitrary canonical metadata is intentionally absent from this public shape.

price_cents.description: Minor units, present only with an explicit currency.

not subscriber-linked. The legacy coupons type is not the deployable

consumer contract is currently wired.

data.description:
Complete rows; one object per row and at most 1 MiB in the compact
persisted JSON representation. PostgreSQL numeric canonicalization
is included in that persisted-size limit.
Runtime validation also bounds field-name length, string bytes,
nesting depth, nested members, total value nodes, and row bytes;
null rows, duplicate JSON keys, non-finite numbers, integers outside
JavaScript's interoperable safe range (-9007199254740991 through
9007199254740991), unsafe controls/bidi formatting in operator-visible
field names, and prototype-pollution keys are rejected. Cell values
preserve legitimate Unicode text, including line/paragraph separators.
NUL characters and malformed/unpaired JSON Unicode surrogate escapes
are rejected before persistence so PostgreSQL and clients cannot
silently mutate the supplied text.
Nonzero decimals are limited to absolute magnitudes from 1e-300 through
1e300. Encode larger numeric identifiers as strings; arbitrary decimals
inside that envelope remain JSON numbers and consumers must not assume
decimal arithmetic is exact.

stored, unattributed — revenue is never dropped merely because its
identity is unknown.
