only for historical reconciliation: an enabled scoped row is
gate-invalid/fail-closed, and a disabled scoped row is unsupported
and inert. NANP phone identity is not recipient-local jurisdiction.

created_at.description: Timestamp in the frozen [2000-01-01, 2100-01-01) projection window.

updated_at.description: Timestamp in the frozen [2000-01-01, 2100-01-01) projection window; never before created_at.

SmsRegistrationResource.description: Legacy provider registration shape. No active A2P operation returns it while registration effects and raw provider receipts are release-held.

SmsSenderInput.description: Sender configuration input. Provider registration identifiers and authoritative pending/approved status are rejected until the durable A2P evidence lifecycle is released.

messaging_service_sid.description: Twilio Messaging Service SID, Telnyx messaging_profile_id, or Bandwidth applicationId.

metadata.description: Only an optional strict quiet_hours policy is accepted.

SmsSenderProfile.description: Minimized tenant sender configuration. It does not prove provider-account ownership, carrier registration approval, callback readiness, or send availability.

brand_registration_sid.description: Historical stored identifier only; A2P submit/poll and authoritative approval are release-held.

campaign_registration_sid.description: Historical stored identifier only; A2P submit/poll and authoritative approval are release-held.

capabilities.description: Empty until provider-derived capability evidence is released; caller values are rejected.

messaging_service_sid.description: Provider sender container identifier: Twilio Messaging Service SID, Telnyx messaging_profile_id, or Bandwidth applicationId.

metadata.description: Allowlisted operational policy only; provider payloads, credentials, arbitrary keys, and operator free text are never projected.

phone_number.description: Provider-owned sender number when direct-number send is used.

provider.description: Provider adapter used for send and callback routing.

phone.description:
Reviewed ASCII US/Canada input. The server removes only ASCII
spaces and the display separators `(`, `)`, `-`, and `.`, accepts
either ten NANP digits or eleven digits beginning with `1`,
validates area/exchange prefixes, and stores/returns canonical
`+1XXXXXXXXXX`. Tabs, newlines, Unicode spacing/digits, letters,
bidi/control marks, and interior or repeated plus signs are rejected.

id.description: Exact deleted suppression or SMS policy row id from the request path.

tenantId.description: Exact authenticated tenant UUID; canonical but not UUIDv4-only.

phone.description:
Reviewed ASCII US/Canada input. The server removes only ASCII
spaces and the display separators `(`, `)`, `-`, and `.`, accepts
either ten NANP digits or eleven digits beginning with `1`,
validates area/exchange prefixes, and stores/returns canonical
`+1XXXXXXXXXX`. Tabs, newlines, Unicode spacing/digits, letters,
bidi/control marks, and interior or repeated plus signs are rejected.

created_at.description: Timestamp in the frozen [2000-01-01, 2100-01-01) projection window.

phone_e164.description: Sensitive exact US/Canada recipient identity. Never place it in a URL, log, or telemetry field.

nextCursor.description: Opaque continuation emitted only with a full requested page and more cutoff rows.

snapshotAt.description: Database response cutoff in the frozen [2000-01-01, 2100-01-01) projection window, shared by every cursor continuation.

tenantId.description: Exact authenticated tenant UUID; canonical but not UUIDv4-only.

total.description: Matching row count at this response cutoff, not a claim about newer state.

enabled_since.description: Start of the current uninterrupted enabled period; reset when a disabled monitor is re-enabled or its interval changes.

first_successful_sync_at.description: First clean sync in the current uninterrupted enabled period.

max_success_gap_seconds.description: Largest observed gap between clean syncs in the current uninterrupted enabled period.

successful_sync_count.description: Clean sync attempts in the current uninterrupted enabled period, including empty polls.

review_evidence.description: Non-secret evidence references attached by an operator.

review_status.description: Independent operator-review state. `reviewed` never implies that the event was automatically applied.

SourcePlatform.description:
Source ESP/CRM we can migrate from. `mailchimp_api` denotes tenants
migrated via the Mailchimp v3 API path (vs `mailchimp` for CSV
export). The gateway returns `mailchimp_api` on subscriber
responses for those tenants.

token.description: HMAC-authenticated, base64-readable URL credential; treat as secret and do not log or persist it.

axis.description: Reserved; the desktop associates the active request axis.

matched_n.description: Number of campaigns in the matching attribute bucket.

count.description: Omitted or zero selects the server default of six; otherwise 5..8.

seed_subject.description: At least 10 UTF-8 bytes after surrounding whitespace is trimmed.

confirmationEmail.description:
Last outcome of the double opt-in email; absent when the submission
has none. `queued` waits to be sent; `sent` was accepted by the
mailer; `send_failed` was refused and is retried; `no_sender` means
the form has no sender on a verified domain and no standard sender
is configured; `quota_exceeded` hit the standard sender's hourly
limit for the workspace and is retried; `recipient_suppressed` is
an address that bounced, complained or was erased.

SubmissionStatus.description:
`pending` awaits the double opt-in click; `confirmed` is subscribed
(single opt-in, or the link was clicked); `unsubscribed` opted out
through the submission; `received` is a response that did not ask to
subscribe (the form's consent checkbox was left unticked).

Subscriber.description:
Tenant-scoped mirror of a Listmonk subscriber, plus Mailchimp-
compatibility fields populated by the import path. The
`mailchimp_*` fields are only meaningful for tenants migrated
from Mailchimp; leave them empty/null for native sign-ups.

account_id.description:
SUB-012 many-to-one link to the first-class accounts object.
null = unlinked (the common B2C case). Set/cleared via
PATCH /api/v1/subscribers/{id}/account. The denormalised
merge_fields.COMPANY pointer is preserved alongside it.

activity_summary.description: Per-event-type latest-timestamp index maintained by the events ingester.

archived_at.description:
Soft-delete marker (SUB-009). null = active. Set by
PATCH /api/v1/subscribers/{id}/archive and cleared by
/unarchive. Archived rows are hidden from list/search by
default (audit-join keys preserved) unless
?include_archived=true is passed. Distinct from the GDPR
hard-erasure DELETE path.

catalog_attributes.description:
SUB-013 catalog-linked profile attributes (favorite_category /
last_viewed_sku), computed from commerce events. Hydrated inline
on the subscriber detail GET so the slideover can show catalog
affinity without a second round-trip. null when the subscriber
has no catalog history yet.

churn_score.description:
SUB-076 cached churn-risk score (migration 0180 smallint column),
now SELECTed on the list/detail response so the column header can
render it and drive a server-side sort (sort=churn). null = never
scored.

consent_ai_processing_at.description:
SUB-041 per-purpose consent vector. State-of-record timestamp of the
last 'granted' consent event for LLM/AI processing. null = no recorded
grant. Read-only.

consent_email_marketing_at.description:
SUB-041 per-purpose consent vector. State-of-record timestamp of the
last 'granted' consent event for email marketing. null = no recorded
grant (treat as denied). Read-only — auto-maintained by the
consent_events trigger; the ledger is the source of truth.

consent_profiling_at.description:
SUB-041 per-purpose consent vector. State-of-record timestamp of the
last 'granted' consent event for analytics / engagement profiling.
null = no recorded grant. Read-only.

consent_sms_marketing_at.description:
SUB-041 per-purpose consent vector. State-of-record timestamp of the
last 'granted' consent event for SMS marketing. null = no recorded
grant. Read-only.

consent_targeted_ads_at.description:
SUB-041 per-purpose consent vector. State-of-record timestamp of the
last 'granted' consent event for sale/share + targeted advertising.
null = no recorded grant. Read-only.

data_region.description:
SUB-052 per-subscriber data-residency override. null = inherit the
owning tenant's data_region (the common case). A non-null value
pins this profile's backups + sub-processor selection to that data
plane; the effective region is resolved by
InheritedRegionFor(subscriber, tenant). Settable via
PATCH /api/v1/subscribers/{id} (send "" to clear the override).

demographics.description:
SUB-063 confidence-labelled inferred-demographics projection (gender /
age_group / interests, each with a model confidence) read from
subscriber_computed_traits under the inferred_* keys. Hydrated inline
only on the subscriber detail GET so the slideover can render a
confidence meter. null on list rows and when no demographic has been
inferred yet. The full read/write surface is at
GET /api/v1/subscribers/{id}/demographics +
PUT /api/v1/subscribers/{id}/traits/inferred_{gender,age_group,interests}.

detected_jurisdiction.description:
SUB-055 ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country inferred from signup_ip by the
jurisdiction detector. null = no detection has run. Compared against
the stored country on upsert to detect a jurisdiction drift.

display_name.description: Operator/UI-facing display label. Defaults to full_name.

engagement_score.description:
SUB-076 cached engagement score (migration 0061 smallint column),
now SELECTed on the list/detail response so the desktop's clickable
column header can render it and drive a server-side sort
(sort=engagement). null = never scored.

expected_next_order_at.description:
SUB-061 replenishment-cadence projection: last_order_at +
average_days_between_orders, derived by the commerce
replenishment-cadence worker and stored on
subscriber_computed_traits (key expected_next_order_at). Hydrated
inline only on the subscriber detail GET so the slideover can show
a "next order expected" projection without a second round-trip.
null on list rows (not hydrated to avoid an N+1 trait fetch) and on
the detail GET when the subscriber has no order history yet. The
full cadence read/write surface is at
GET/PATCH /api/v1/subscribers/{id}/replenishment-cadence.

external_id.description:
Operator-supplied external identifier (e.g. Shopify customer ID,
CRM record ID). Unique per tenant when set. Drives the
/subscribers/identify upsert path so an integration can stitch
anonymous → known without depending on email as the join key.

federated_master_id.description:
SUB-023 cross-tenant master identity link. When this child-workspace
subscriber (in an agency/MSP hierarchy) is federated to a master
subscriber in the parent workspace, this carries the parent's
master_subscriber_id. null = not federated. Managed via
/api/v1/subscribers/{id}/federated-links.

first_name.description:
Given name, promoted to a first-class column (SUB-004) so it can
be sorted (sort=first_name) and used in picker UIs. Populated from
merge_fields.FNAME (Mailchimp) / custom_fields.first_name
(Klaviyo) when not supplied explicitly. Empty string when unknown.

frequency_preference.description:
SUB-132 subscriber-level send-cadence hint (migration 0180 column):
'default' | 'weekly' | 'monthly' | 'paused'. Chosen via the
smart-unsubscribe flow or set directly via
PATCH /api/v1/subscribers/{id}. Read at send time by the queue-fill
frequency filter so a 'paused' subscriber (whose paused_until is null
or in the future) is excluded from the campaign audience. Always
present (the column is NOT NULL DEFAULT 'default').

full_name.description: Convenience "first last" name. Derived when not supplied.

gpp_sections.description:
SUB-120 per-jurisdiction IAB Global Privacy Platform (GPP) section
strings, stored verbatim (no decoding in this phase), e.g.
{"usnat":"BAAAAAA...","usca":"BAAAAAA..."}. Populated only by the
GPP reads/ingest (GET/POST/PATCH /api/v1/subscribers/{id}/gpp);
omitted on the standard list/detail projection. {} / absent = none
on file.

jurisdiction_changed_at.description:
SUB-055 timestamp of the most recent detected jurisdiction drift
(inferred jurisdiction != stored country). null = no drift recorded.

jurisdiction_reconfirm_required.description:
SUB-055 flag: true when a drift into a stricter consent regime
(GDPR / CASL / Quebec Law 25) requires a fresh consent
re-confirmation. Cleared by
PATCH /api/v1/subscribers/{id}/jurisdiction-reconfirm.

last_name.description:
Family name, first-class column (SUB-004). Sortable via
sort=last_name. Populated from merge_fields.LNAME /
custom_fields.last_name when not supplied. Empty when unknown.

mailchimp_last_changed.description: Last-modified timestamp from Mailchimp's source-of-truth (used to gate suppression writes — see internal/listmonk_events).

order_cadence_metrics.description:
SUB-062 compact repeat-purchase projection (average_days_between_orders
+ last_computed_at), read from the same average_days_between_orders
computed trait the replenishment-cadence worker maintains. Hydrated
inline only on the subscriber detail GET so the slideover can render a
"Repeat Purchase Behavior" card. null on list rows and when no cadence
has been computed yet.

paused_until.description:
SUB-132 temporary-suppression auto-reactivation timestamp (migration
0180 column). When frequency_preference='paused', a non-null
paused_until in the future means "skip this subscriber until then";
a null paused_until with frequency_preference='paused' means "paused
indefinitely". Settable via PATCH /api/v1/subscribers/{id} (send
paused_until to set, or clear_paused_until=true to clear). SUB-135
vacation mode adds a pause_days convenience on the same PATCH: a
value 1..365 computes paused_until = now + pause_days and pins
frequency_preference to 'paused' when unset (out-of-range 422s;
mutually exclusive with clear_paused_until). null in the common
non-paused case.

prediction.description:
SUB-059 first-class predictive-CLV projection (historic / predicted /
total CLV in cents) plus churn risk and the SUB-060 explainable churn
drivers. Hydrated only on the detail GET via a LEFT JOIN on
profile_predictions (migrations 0206 + 0912, populated by the
predictive worker). null on list rows (not hydrated to avoid an N+1
join) and on the detail GET when the predictive worker has not scored
this subscriber's email yet. The same projection is served standalone
at GET /api/v1/predictive/profiles/{email}.

prediction_confidence.description:
SUB-010 model confidence in [0,1] for the current cached predictive
score (migration 0900). null = the model declined to score under its
minimum-data threshold, or no model has scored this subscriber.
Hydrated only on the detail GET alongside prediction_model_version.

prediction_model_version.description:
SUB-010 predictive-score model lineage (migration 0900). The
freeform model version (e.g. "heuristic-v1", "churn-xgb-v2") behind
the cached churn/engagement scalar, surfaced for the Klaviyo-style
explainability badge. Hydrated only on the detail GET (the churn
snapshot wins when both churn + engagement metadata exist); absent
on list rows and when no model has scored this subscriber. The full
per-feature snapshot + per-score-type history is at
GET /api/v1/subscribers/{id}/prediction-metadata. Writable via
PATCH /api/v1/subscribers/{id} (model_version + confidence) or the
dedicated PATCH /api/v1/subscribers/{id}/prediction-metadata.

preference_topics.description:
SUB-134 per-topic opt-in state for this subscriber, hydrated only on
the detail GET (null on list rows to avoid an N+1 topics fetch). Each
entry pairs a tenant topic with the subscriber's current opt-in state
(defaulting to the topic's default_opt_in when the subscriber has no
explicit row). null when no topics are configured. The full read/write
surface is at GET/PUT /api/v1/subscribers/{email}/topics.

primary_email.description:
SUB-016 canonical contact address. A profile may own up to 5
addresses (see SubscriberEmail / /api/v1/subscribers/{id}/emails);
exactly one is the primary, and its value is mirrored here on
subscribers.primary_email. Defaults to email on creation and is
re-pointed when a different address is promoted via the multi-email
set-primary path. Empty only on legacy rows scanned before the
column existed.

profile_id.description:
SUB-017 stable synthetic profile identifier, distinct from the
physical row `id`. Top of the identifier precedence hierarchy
(profile_id > external_id > email > phone > anonymous): an
/subscribers/identify call that resolves a profile_id wins
outright, before external_id / email / phone are consulted.
Auto-assigned on creation; stable across merges.

rating.description:
SUB-076 Mailchimp-parity contact rating, 1..5 stars (migration 0226
smallint column), now SELECTed on the list/detail response so the
column header can render it and drive a server-side sort
(sort=rating). null = unrated.

signup_ip.description: Originating IP at signup (best-effort, may be empty).

version.description:
Strong optimistic-concurrency token for this exact subscriber
representation. Echo it in If-Match on mutation surfaces that
require compare-and-swap; never synthesize, weaken, or reuse it
after a refresh or conflicting write.

SubscriberAccountLinkInput.description: Sets a first-class account UUID or clears the link with null, omission, or a blank string.

account_id.description: Tenant-visible account UUID; null or a blank value clears the current link.

SubscriberAlias.description:
One tenant-scoped alternate identifier owned by exactly one subscriber
profile. subscriber_version and external_id are mutation projections:
subscriber_version is the fresh parent revision to chain into the next
write, while external_id reports the resulting canonical external link.

alias_type.description: Email/phone may appear only on legacy read rows; direct alias writes reject those contact-method types.

external_id.description: Canonical external_id after the mutation. Omitted on ordinary list rows.

subscriber_version.description: Fresh strong parent-subscriber revision returned by a successful mutation and repeated in ETag.

external_id.description: Canonical external_id after deletion; null when the deleted alias was the canonical link.

subscriber_id.description: Canonical subscriber UUID whose alias was removed.

subscriber_version.description: Fresh strong parent-subscriber revision, repeated in ETag.
Strong parent-subscriber revision observed with this list and repeated in ETag.

SubscriberAttributeHistoryEvent.description: One per-field before/after change in the SUB-008 attribute history log.

changed_by.description: Actor UUID when known; omitted otherwise.

field_name.description:
Logical field that changed. Scalar columns use the column name
("status", "locale"); jsonb map keys use a dotted path
("custom_fields.phone", "merge_fields.FNAME").

new_value.description: Rendered new value; null when the field was removed.

old_value.description: Rendered prior value; null when the field was absent before.

next_cursor.description: RFC3339 timestamp to pass as ?before for the next page; empty on the last page.

SubscriberAuditLogEntry.description:
One row of the subscriber-scoped audit trail (SUB-123). A thin
projection of the audit_log table mirroring the global
GET /api/v1/audit field set so SIEM ingest can reuse one parser.

list_id.description:
The list to add the audience to, in either of its two forms:
its numeric `id` from `GET /api/v1/lists` (what the dashboard
and apps send), or its `postwave_uuid`. The server resolves
either form to the list; a canonical positive integer or a
canonical hyphenated UUID is required (`invalid_list_id`
otherwise), and a list this workspace does not have — never
created, or deleted — is `404 list_not_found`. Nothing is
written for an id that does not resolve.

A contact who was removed from the list is added back. Ids in
the audience that were already members, or that name no
contact in this workspace, are counted in `skipped` and broken
down in `exclusions` (`already_on_list`,
`missing_or_outside_tenant`).

SubscriberBulkListInput.description:
Audience plus the one list to add it to. Serves both
`bulk/add-to-list` and `bulk/move-to-list`, which are the same handler.

SubscriberBulkMergeInput.description:
SUB-020 bulk-merge request. Up to 500 primary/duplicate pairs; each
runs in its own transaction.

SubscriberBulkMergeItem.description: One pair's outcome within a bulk merge.

error.description: Stable error code when status=failed (e.g. same_subscriber).

SubscriberBulkMergeResult.description:
SUB-020 bulk-merge outcome. merged + failed sum to the number of input
pairs; items carries the per-pair status so failures can be retried in
isolation.

SubscriberBulkTarget.description: Exactly one explicit subscriber-id list or saved segment must be supplied.

subscriber_version.description: Exact parent-subscriber revision, byte-for-byte equal to the response ETag.

SubscriberEmail.description:
SUB-016 — one of up to 5 addresses attached to a profile. Each address
carries independent consent / suppression / engagement state and rolls
up to a single subscriber. Exactly one address per profile is the
primary (canonical contact) address, mirrored onto
subscribers.primary_email.

consent_status.description:
Per-address consent state, independent of the profile. SUB-044
adds never_subscribed as the explicit third state (the address was
added but the contact has never opted in), distinct from unknown
(no recorded signal either way).

is_primary.description: Whether this is the canonical contact address.

last_engaged_at.description: Last engagement timestamp for this specific address.

suppressed.description: Per-address suppression flag, independent of the profile.

version.description: Strong per-address revision, byte-for-byte equal to the response ETag.

SubscriberEmailAddInput.description:
Exact address-attachment body. Omitting `consent_status` defaults the
address to `never_subscribed` and requires every provenance field to be
absent. Any explicit status, including `never_subscribed`, requires the
complete reviewed provenance tuple. Unknown fields are ignored by the
current compatibility decoder.

is_primary.description: A true value cannot rotate an existing canonical address and returns 409 once an address row exists.

occurred_at.description: Reviewed event time; values more than five minutes in the future are rejected.

SubscriberEmailVersion.description: Exact quoted strong revision derived from this address row's ID and microsecond-resolution update time.

SubscriberEngagementResult.description:
Per-subscriber Contact Performance Report (SUB-125). Engagement
score (0-100) plus a counts rollup over a trailing 90-day window,
including currency-safe conversion revenue for the recipient over
the same window. Revenue is never summed across currencies.

clicks_30d.description: Clicks over the smaller trailing 30-day window.

mixed_currency.description: True when revenue_by_currency has more than one entry.

revenue_by_currency.description:
Exact recognized-currency totals, ordered by revenue
descending, monetary conversion count descending, then ISO
code ascending. Always an array and empty when there is no
safely-denominated revenue.

revenue_cents_saturated.description:
True when this currency's exact sum exceeds the int64
wire range and revenue_cents is clamped.

revenue_cents.description:
Revenue in revenue_currency only; 0 when there is no valid
monetary conversion. For mixed-currency windows this is the
deterministic dominant-currency total (highest revenue, then
monetary conversion count, then ISO code), never a
cross-currency sum.

revenue_cents_saturated.description:
True when the exact dominant-currency sum exceeds the int64
wire range and revenue_cents is clamped to the nearest bound.

revenue_currency.description:
ISO-4217 denomination of revenue_cents. Omitted when the
window has no amount-bearing conversion with a recognized
currency.

unclassified_monetary_conversions.description:
Number of amount-bearing conversions whose denomination is
missing or not recognized by the ISO-4217 registry. Their
amounts are deliberately excluded from every revenue total.

opens_30d.description: Opens over the smaller trailing 30-day window.

SubscriberFunnel.description:
Subscriber cohort funnel (SUB-128): signup → first-purchase →
repeat-purchase, bucketed by signup-month cohort. Conversions are
computed from commerce_orders joined to subscribers by
case-insensitive email. Only currently paid orders on or after signup
and through the query snapshot qualify. Counts are lifetime-to-date;
newer cohorts have had less time to convert.

SubscriberFunnelStep.description: One labeled stage in the aggregate subscriber funnel (SUB-128).

added.description: Profiles created on this UTC date that remain unarchived at evaluation time; this is not a gross historical ingest count.

date.description: UTC snapshot date. Points are strictly ascending and never in the future.

evaluated_at.description: Database evaluation time on the same UTC date; never later than the response read/write time.

lapsed.description: Unavailable placeholder only. No canonical engagement-decay definition is configured; clients must exclude this field because unavailable_metrics contains lapsed.

total.description: Unarchived subscriber profiles at evaluation time; archived and merged tombstones are excluded.

unsubbed.description: Verified lower bound of distinct profiles with a paired exact-address granted-to-withdrawn transition from supported profile-wide writers on this UTC date. Later profile archival or address maintenance does not erase a qualifying immutable transition. See partial_metrics; legacy and unbound withdrawal paths are excluded.

delta.description: Newest total minus oldest total; zero when fewer than two points exist.

delta_pct.description: delta / oldest total × 100; zero when fewer than two points exist or the oldest total is zero.

metric_contract_version.description: Closed semantic contract for every point in series. Legacy heuristic history is deliberately excluded rather than relabelled or backfilled.

note.description: Human-readable UTC scope, partial-coverage, unavailable-metric, and cold-start disclosure.

partial_metrics.description: Verified lower-bound flows whose source coverage is intentionally non-exhaustive. A metric cannot appear in both partial_metrics and unavailable_metrics.

total_unsubbed.description: Sum of the verified lower-bound unsubbed points; not the tenant's exhaustive unsubscribe total.

unavailable_metrics.description: Placeholder-valued flows that clients must omit from charts, totals, anomaly detection, accessible tables, and exports.

error.description: Privacy-safe diagnostic without an email address or raw uploaded row.

error_code.description: Stable failure classification, or an empty string for a legacy row.

row_number.description: One-based CSV data-row number recorded by the import worker.

SubscriberImportTemplate.description: SUB-109 — a saved, reusable CSV-import column-mapping template.

mapping.description: Column->field mapping, same shape as the import preview mapping.

source_hint.description: Optional free-text label for the source this mapping fits.

SubscriberLifecycle.description:
One subscriber-aggregate lifecycle projection. subscriber_version is
the exact strong parent revision repeated in the response ETag.
transitioned fields are present only on a write that changed stage.

previous_stage.description: Previous effective stage when this write transitioned stage.

subscriber_version.description: Exact strong parent-subscriber revision, repeated in ETag.

payload.description: Seed stats + feature dims + similarity-band breakdown.

SubscriberLookalikeDetail.description:
SUB-068 response for GET /api/v1/subscribers/lookalike/{id}: aggregate
header plus an opt-in page of ranked members.

pii_included.description: True only when direct subscriber identities were explicitly requested.

SubscriberLookalikeExportInput.description:
SUB-068 body to associate a lookalike audience with a configured
audience_destinations target. This does not start delivery.

destination_id.description: A configured, tenant-owned audience_destinations id to associate.

SubscriberLookalikeInput.description:
SUB-068 first-party lookalike-audience generation request
(subscriber-namespaced). The audience is built by ranking non-seed
subscribers by first-party similarity to the seed segment's members.

confidence_threshold.description: Drop candidates below this similarity floor; null = no floor.

data_use_acknowledged.description: Explicit acknowledgement of the first-party modeling data-use notice.

name.description: Optional display name for the generated audience.

seed_segment_id.description: The segment whose members define the lookalike seed.

SubscriberMergeInput.description:
SUB-019 single-merge request. The duplicate is merged into the
primary; ids are subscriber row ids (not emails).

duplicate_id.description: The subscriber to merge in and delete.

primary_id.description: The surviving subscriber's id (wins on conflict).

signals.description:
SUB-025 optional identity-resolution evidence behind this merge.
Each entry records which heuristic judged the two profiles the
same person and at what confidence; they are persisted to a
per-merge audit table in the same transaction as the merge.

SubscriberMergeResult.description: SUB-019 merge outcome — what moved from the duplicate to the primary.

custom_fields_merged.description: custom_fields key count on the merged row after union.

events_moved.description: subscriber_events rows re-pointed to the primary's email.

signals_recorded.description:
SUB-025 count of identity-resolution signal rows persisted to the
per-merge audit log. Zero when no signals were supplied.

suppressions_moved.description: suppression rows re-pointed to the primary's email.

tags_merged.description: Tag count on the merged row after union.

SubscriberMergeSignal.description:
SUB-025 one identity-resolution signal that contributed to a merge
decision (e.g. case_diff, plus_alias, dot_alias, external_id_claim,
manual).

confidence.description: Per-signal confidence in [0,1]. Omit when not scored.

kind.description: The signal/heuristic that fired. Application-owned vocabulary.

metadata.description: Optional structured context (matched value, normaliser version, ...).

SubscriberNote.description:
SUB-097 — an operator-authored note on a subscriber. body is the
plain-text projection (search / legacy clients); markdown_body is the
rich source the composer round-trips, with @-mentions stored inline as
`@[Name](user:id)` tokens. mentions and attachments are denormalised
for the pane. Notes are operator-only context, never subscriber-visible.

body.description: Plain-text projection of markdown_body (mention tokens collapsed to @Name).

markdown_body.description: Rich markdown source, including inline @[Name](user:id) mention tokens.

SubscriberNoteAttachment.description:
SUB-097 — a file attached to a subscriber note. Bytes live in the
tenant-scoped object store; this row carries the metadata + storage
key. On list, download_url is a short-lived presigned GET URL.

download_url.description: Short-lived presigned GET URL. Present only on list responses.

file_key.description: Tenant-relative object-store key the bytes live under.

SubscriberNoteMention.description:
SUB-097 — one @-mention extracted from a note's markdown body. Stored
inline in markdown_body as an `@[Display](user:UUID)` token and
denormalised into mentions_json so "notes that mention me" can query
by containment.

display.description: The display text the author typed for the mention.

user_id.description: The mentioned teammate's user id (lower-cased UUID).

SubscriberParentVersion.description: Exact quoted strong parent-subscriber revision derived from the canonical subscriber row.

SubscriberPrediction.description:
SUB-059 subscriber-level predictive payload surfaced on the detail GET.
A read-only projection of the profile_predictions row keyed on
(tenant, email) — the same row /api/v1/predictive serves — narrowed to
the three CLV figures, churn risk, and the SUB-060 explainable churn
drivers. Populated only when the predictive worker has scored this
address.

calculated_at.description: When the predictive worker last scored this profile.

churn_drivers.description:
SUB-060 ranked top-3 explainable churn drivers, highest impact first.
Empty when no driver crosses the salience floor.

data_sufficiency.description: How much signal the model had for this profile.

historic_clv_cents.description: Realised lifetime value to date, in cents.

predicted_clv_cents.description: Modelled forward lifetime value, in cents.

total_clv_cents.description: Historic + predicted, in cents — the headline CLV.

max_archived.description: Cap on archived rows kept per tenant. 0 = no cap.

retention_days.description: Days an archived row is kept before the reconciler may hard-purge it. 0 = never.

SubscriberSuppressInput.description: Optional suppression evidence for the already-loaded canonical address; reason/source default to manual.

subscriber_id.description: Request identity echoed by the current aggregator; callers may have supplied a UUID or email.

detail.description: Source-specific structured detail; omitted when the event carries no detail.

source.description: Canonical backing event source used in the composite cursor ordering.

type.description: Stable event vocabulary from the selected source family.

before.description: The effective legacy/composite cursor timestamp; omitted on the first page.

next_cursor.description: Opaque continuation emitted only when `has_more` is true.

click_rate.description: Overall clicked event count divided by sent count; repeated events can make this exceed one.

engagement_daily_30d.description: Oldest-to-newest UTC engagement counts for the fixed trailing 30-day window.

last_active_at.description: Omitted when no engagement or reply activity exists.

open_rate.description: Overall opened event count divided by sent count; repeated events can make this exceed one.

SubscriberTopicView.description:
SUB-134 — one tenant topic with the subscriber's resolved opt-in state,
as surfaced under Subscriber.preference_topics on the detail GET.

default_opt_in.description:
The topic's default opt-in state for subscribers with no explicit
subscriber_topics row.

display_order.description: The topic's sort order in the preference center.

name.description: Human-readable topic name rendered in the preference center.

opted_in.description:
The subscriber's resolved opt-in state (their explicit
subscriber_topics value, or the topic default when unset).

SubscriptionDisconnectCleanupEvidence.description: Operator-managed provider cleanup readiness evidence returned for Recharge disconnects. Moosewave marks the local row disconnected and records cleanup guidance; provider-console API-token/webhook cleanup remains operator-managed until managed cleanup automation is certified.

SubscriptionInput.description: Canonical Moosewave subscription row. This is not a raw provider webhook payload.

credentials_ref.description: Vault or envelope reference identifier. Raw credential material in settings or this field is rejected.

scopes.description: Ignored for subscription/shipping ingest foundations; official scopes are attached only by verified provider adapters.

SubscriptionLifecycleEventInput.description: Canonical Moosewave subscription/shipping lifecycle event row. This is not a raw provider webhook payload.

SubscriptionProviderCleanupAcknowledgeme.description: Local operator attestation that Recharge provider-console cleanup actions were reviewed or completed. Accepted action keys include `api_token_revoked_or_rotated`, `webhook_target_or_subscription_removed_or_disabled`, `tokenized_ingest_urls_removed`, `duplicate_or_manual_webhook_targets_audited`, and `provider_console_cleanup_reviewed_no_action_due`.

scopes.description: Official provider scopes only. Empty for subscription/shipping ingest foundations until provider pullers are verified.

sync_model.description: Moosewave execution model. `postwave_subscription_ingest` means the route imports canonical subscription, shipment, and lifecycle event rows and does not imply provider API polling.

sync_objects.description: Canonical Moosewave ingest objects exposed by this surface. Subscription/shipping foundations expose subscriptions, shipments, and events only until provider API pullers are verified.

verification_mode.description: Current provider-authenticity posture. Subscription/shipping ingest foundations use `postwave_ingest_token` until provider raw-body verification is wired into the route.

webhook_topics.description: Official provider topics only when a raw-body verifier and provider webhook handler exists.

SubscriptionShipmentInput.description: Canonical Moosewave shipment row. This is not a raw provider webhook payload.

SubscriptionSyncRequest.description: Imports canonical subscription rows when `subscriptions`, `shipments`, or `events` are provided. Providers with native pullers, such as Recharge, may accept an empty request plus optional cursor to trigger provider-managed subscription polling.

provider.description:
Bounded provider slug stored on this historical record. It may be a
sanitized long-tail slug absent from the current static provider
catalog and never implies credential, callback, sync, or runtime
availability.

SupportProviderListResponse.description:
The current static, release-held provider catalog. `complete: true` means
this catalog page is not paginated; it does not claim to enumerate every
bounded provider slug that may exist on a sanitized historical record.

SuppressionEntry.description: One row of the consolidated suppression list (subscriber_suppressions, the X1 source of truth). SUB-047/SUB-048.

bounce_category.description: SUB-048 — durable raw classification the bounce-ingest receiver derived from provider codes + metadata at ingest time. Survives a later operator reclassification of `reason`. Null for manual adds.

expires_at.description: When set, the suppression auto-clears once this instant passes; the retention sweeper (SUB-049) hard-deletes the row after expiry. Null = permanent.

source.description: Provider / surface that wrote the suppression.

color.description: Strict writes use TagWriteColor; a bounded historical value can be returned unchanged.

description.description: Strict writes allow 1024 characters; bounded historical rows up to 4096 remain readable.

etag.description: Exact strong tag token, repeated in the ETag response header on singular writes.

name.description: Strict writes allow 64 characters; bounded historical rows up to 100 remain readable.
Strict writes allow 64 characters; bounded historical rows up to 100 remain readable.

sort_order.description: Strict writes allow 0 through 1,000,000; historical signed values remain readable.

next_cursor.description: Empty on the terminal page; otherwise echo verbatim in the next request.

TagWriteColor.description: Empty clears the color; otherwise use a supported palette id or CSS hex triplet/sextet.

click_rate.description: Clicks divided by sent events, rounded to four decimals.

open_rate.description: Opens divided by sent events, rounded to four decimals.

event_type.description: Payload event_type when present, otherwise the bus topic.

topic.description: Server bus topic used as the SSE event name.

ts.description: RFC 3339 nanosecond timestamp retained for SDK compatibility.

campaign_id.description: Optional — defaults to URL path param.

subject.description: Override subject for the test send only.

TrackingConsent.description:
Recipient-level email tracking consent. Timestamp presence represents
an explicit per-dimension opt-out. Effective values additionally honour
Global Privacy Control, so `gpc=true` makes both effective values true
without fabricating explicit opt-out timestamps.

click_opt_out_at.description: Present only when click tracking was explicitly opted out.

effective_click_opt_out.description: Send-time click-rewrite suppression after explicit preference and GPC are combined.

effective_open_opt_out.description: Send-time open-tracking suppression after explicit preference and GPC are combined.

gpc.description: Recorded Global Privacy Control signal; true suppresses both tracking modes.

open_opt_out_at.description: Present only when open tracking was explicitly opted out.

subscriber_email.description: Current server-resolved email; callers never choose it on the stable route.

subscriber_id.description: Stable subscriber identity used by the primary endpoint and version token.

version.description: Exact strong revision token to send as If-Match. It is carried in the body because sensitive responses strip ETag cache validators.

TrackingConsentPatch.description:
Partial tracking-consent update. Supply at least one of open_opt_out,
click_opt_out, or gpc; an empty object is accepted only when the request
carries `Sec-GPC: 1`. Omitted source/policy values inherit the existing
evidence (or default to admin/v1 on first write). Explicit empty values,
unknown fields, control/format characters, oversized strings, trailing
JSON, and bodies over 2 KiB are rejected. A `Sec-GPC: 1` request is
forced to gpc=true with source=gpc even if the body attempts otherwise.

click_opt_out.description: Set/clear the explicit click-tracking opt-out timestamp.

gpc.description: Record/clear the GPC projection. Sec-GPC:1 always wins and records true.

open_opt_out.description: Set/clear the explicit open-tracking opt-out timestamp.

policy_version.description: Policy identifier, limited to both 100 UTF-8 bytes and 100 Unicode scalar values.

source.description: Bounded evidence source such as admin, preference_center, or gpc.

confidence.description: Historical metadata; not proof of an active learner.

sample_count.description: Historical metadata; not proof of an active learner.

expectedUpdatedAt.description: Optional only for legacy-client compatibility; web sends the reviewed revision.

UpdateCampaignInput.description: All authoring fields are optional; nil/missing means leave unchanged. Dispatch lifecycle fields are intentionally absent.

content_blocks.description: Complete replacement authoring tree. Semantic trees are strict- decoded, normalized, and never converted through legacy HTML.

list_id.description: Send to one list: its numeric id or the list's uuid (`postwave_uuid` on list responses), resolved within the workspace and stored by numeric id. An empty string clears it. To switch a campaign between a list and a segment, send both fields with the unused one empty. Once a campaign has started sending, or its audience has been frozen, its list can no longer change (409 campaign_dispatching or audience_frozen).

segment_id.description: Send to one segment. An empty string clears it.

UpdateChannelConsentInput.description:
SUB-042 PATCH body for /api/v1/subscribers/{id}/channel-consents/{channel}.
A frequency-cap-only edit may omit status. An opted_in/opted_out status
requires the complete evidence tuple below; those evidence fields are
rejected without status and cannot be attached to pending/unknown.

clear_frequency_cap.description: When true, drops the frequency cap (sets it null). Distinguishes "clear" from "unchanged".

status.description: Reviewed email decision. Omit for a frequency-cap-only edit; non-email status mutations currently return 422 fail-closed.

UpdateDeduplicationSettingsInput.description: SUB-021 PUT body. merge_confidence_threshold must be in [0,1].

UpdateIdentifierTransformInput.description:
SUB-018 PATCH body. Every field is optional; an omitted field leaves
the current value unchanged. At least one field is required.

UpdateSequenceRequest.description:
Partial draft-authoring update. `emails`, `steps`, and `ops` are
mutually exclusive when present. Empty `emails` or `steps` arrays
intentionally clear the sequence canvas. `goal: null` clears the goal;
omitted fields retain their current value. `status: archived` must be
the only property in the request. Unknown fields and semantic no-op
patches are rejected with 400 and do not increment the row version.
The resulting recursive canvas is bounded to 100 total nodes and depth 3.

reason.description: Optional operator rationale retained in lifecycle transition history; never copied into the automation outbox payload.

source.description: Reviewed machine/operator surface that originated the change.

UpdateSubscriberNoteInput.description:
SUB-097 PATCH body for /api/v1/subscribers/{id}/notes/{note}. At least
one of pinned / markdown_body must be present. Editing markdown_body
re-syncs the plain body projection and the extracted mentions.

UpsertSubscriberAliasInput.description:
An ordinary non-contact identity alias. Email and phone are
intentionally absent: those destinations require their verified
contact-method workflows so alias management cannot bypass consent.

currency.description: Optional caller currency, normalized to uppercase.

customer_email.description: Accepted for commerce-system compatibility, then discarded without persistence or attribution.

occurred_at.description: Optional source occurrence time; defaults to server time.

weight.description: Sampling weight; values are normalized server-side.

emails.description: Addresses to verify synchronously in one bounded provider wave; duplicate accounting is returned in `usage`.

health_summary.description: Closed A/B/C/D/F/U counts, including zero-valued keys.

emails.description:
Addresses are normalized and de-duplicated. Each raw value is
validated before any database lock is acquired; whole-cache
invalidation is intentionally unavailable.

note.description: Present when the tenant has no paid provider configured.

ambiguous.description: Provider dispatches whose outcome is terminally unknown and must not be retried automatically.

attempts.description: Durable worker claim attempts recorded for the job.

created_by.description: Acting session user when creation used a user session; omitted for API-key callers and after retention scrubbing.

error.description: Sanitized operator-facing terminal failure message; raw provider or persistence errors are never returned.

failure_code.description: Stable public-safe terminal failure code, present only when one applies.

source_ref.description: Normalized, bounded, public-safe source handle; malformed legacy values are omitted.

VerificationJobCreateRequest.description:
Strict bulk-job input. `source` is trimmed and defaults to `inline`.
Address values are trimmed, lower-cased, blank values removed, and
duplicates collapsed in first-seen order before the durable request
fingerprint and job items are written. Bounds marked in UTF-8 bytes are
enforced by the runtime in addition to the JSON Schema character bounds.

emails.description:
Required and non-empty for `inline` and `upload`; empty or omitted
for `tag` and `all_subscribers`. Each normalized value is at most
320 UTF-8 bytes and may still resolve to a syntax-invalid terminal
verification result.

source_ref.description:
Optional single-line source handle. It is required and non-blank
for `tag`; it must be blank or omitted for `all_subscribers`.
The schema excludes controls and unsafe BMP format, separator,
surrogate, and private-use ranges; the runtime additionally rejects
the complete Unicode Cf/Co/Cs/Zl/Zp categories.

VerificationJobExecutionMode.description: Immutable verification tier frozen when the durable job is created.

health.description: Optional additive tenant-derived health decision for this persisted result.

status.description: Canonical verification status, or an empty string while the item is pending.

VerificationJobSource.description:
Address provenance resolved transactionally when the job is created.
`inline` and `upload` use the request's `emails`; `tag` resolves
`source_ref`; `all_subscribers` resolves the complete tenant pool.

VerificationMode.description: Off performs no policy verification, local uses only free checks, and full may spend provider credits.

forms_reject_statuses.description:
Empty or omitted selects the terminal-invalid default set. Duplicate
rejectable statuses are collapsed in first-seen order. `valid` is
affirmative evidence and can never be configured as a rejection rule.

warning.description: Present when full enforcement is saved without a configured provider.

credential_ref.description: Opaque tenant-local credential identifier; never API-key material.

last_error.description: Bounded public-safe provider health message; raw upstream or secret-resolution detail is never returned.

cache_ttl_days.description: Zero selects the 30-day default; positive values override it up to 180 days.

degrade_on_failure.description: Whether advisory bulk verification may retain local-only results after a pre-dispatch provider failure.

ip_address.description: Optional provider source IPv4 or IPv6 address.

credential_ref.description: Opaque tenant-local credential identifier resolved only inside the server-owned tenant/provider namespace.

email.description: Address to verify. Syntax failures are returned as an invalid verification result.

billable.description: True when this result consumed a paid provider credit.

cached.description: True when the verification verdict came from tenant cache.

health.description:
Optional tenant-derived decision. It is additive for backward
compatibility. Inspect `evidence_complete` before trusting the
recommendation as a complete evidence view.

sub_status.description: Provider/local fine-grained reason; omitted when no sub-status applies.

VerificationStatusSummary.description: Counts keyed by canonical verification status; absent statuses have no entry.

email_position.description:
Set only for regeneration jobs; the 0-indexed position of
the email being regenerated. Null for first-generation runs.

sequence_id.description:
Populated on `succeeded`. For regeneration jobs the field is
pre-set at create time to the target sequence; for first-
generation jobs it appears once the run lands.

VoiceSource.description: Least-privilege source summary. Raw ingestion parameters, corpus text, tenant identifiers, archive paths, connector metadata, and URL query values are intentionally omitted from list responses.

label.description: Safe display label; feed URLs omit query and fragment values.

confirmation_name.description: Must exactly equal the current connection name after surrounding whitespace is trimmed.

WarehouseExpectedVersion.description: Zero is create-only; a positive value must exactly match the current mapping version.

WarehouseNativeConnection.description: Safe public connection projection. Credential references, last cursor, raw error, and provider cleanup evidence are deliberately absent.

config.description: Recursively sanitized non-secret provider settings; credential and provider_cleanup keys are absent.
Provider settings only; raw secrets, endpoint overrides, and provider_cleanup are not public inputs.

credentials_ref.description: Vault or envelope reference; raw credential material is rejected. Forbidden for streaming_export.

WarehouseNativeHealth.description: Safe health projection; raw errors and warning strings are replaced by boolean/count evidence.

WarehouseNativeProviderHealth.description: Safe provider-probe projection; SQL statements, messages, warnings, and raw errors are absent.

state.description: Provider-health probe state such as ready, not_ready, driver_not_attached, checked, provider_checked, or failed.

WarehouseNativeRun.description: Safe public run projection. Input/output URIs, cursors, internal metrics, and raw error are deliberately absent.

run_mode.description: Use manual for an on-demand sync; the legacy `sync` alias is normalized server-side but is not part of the new contract.

WarehouseProviderCleanupAcknowledgementI.description: Version-bound local Snowflake cleanup attestation. At least one completed action or non-empty note is required.

confirmation_target.description: Must exactly match the current target_field_key after surrounding whitespace is trimmed.

WarehouseRowErrorEvidence.description: Redacted row-error evidence; error_message and raw_row are deliberately absent.

WarehouseStreamingConfig.description: Public streaming-export config. Storage is tenant-bound; bucket and destination credentials are never accepted.

WarehouseStreamingRun.description: Safe streaming-run projection. Object storage URI and raw error are deliberately absent.

notify_auto_disabled.description: Notify after the canonical outbound worker auto-pauses a destination.

notify_failure_rate.description: Retained compatibility threshold; not yet evaluated against canonical outbound deliveries.

notify_latency.description: Retained compatibility threshold; not yet evaluated against canonical outbound deliveries.

WebhookEvent.description:
One event inside the delivered envelope.

Corrected against the dispatcher that actually builds it
(`outbound_webhooks/dispatcher.go:266-273`), which emits exactly
`{id, type, occurred_at, data}`.

This schema previously said `created_at` and included `tenant_id`.
Neither is sent. A subscriber written from the old schema would read
`event.created_at` as undefined on every delivery and could wait for a
`tenant_id` that never arrives — and because both are silent absences
rather than errors, nothing would have reported it. The tenant is
identified on the transport envelope, not inside the event.

occurred_at.description: When the event happened, RFC3339 UTC as written by the dispatcher.

WebhookSubscription.description:
The public projection of an outbound webhook.

This schema listed six properties while the gateway returns twenty-one
(`outbound_webhooks.Webhook`). The missing fifteen were not optional
detail: `consecutive_failures`, `disabled_reason` and `disabled_at` are
how a subscriber learns their endpoint has been switched off, and the
signing-key fields are how they verify a payload without contacting us.
A client generated from the old schema could not see any of it.

Private signing material is still absent, and deliberately: the HMAC
secret and private key are returned ONCE at create/rotate and never in
this projection. `secret` below is therefore create-only, not a field
present on a fetched subscription.

auth_config.description: Outbound auth for the endpoint. Secrets within are redacted on read.

auth_config_status.description:
Whether the stored outbound-auth material is usable — the field a
subscriber checks when deliveries start failing authentication,
since the config itself comes back redacted.

consecutive_failures.description: Consecutive delivery failures; drives automatic disabling.

secondary_public_key.description: The incoming key during a rotation overlap, so a subscriber can accept both.

secret.description:
Plaintext signing secret, returned ONLY in the create and rotate
responses. Absent from every read — it is envelope-encrypted at rest
and cannot be retrieved again.

signing_algorithm.description: HMAC, ECDSA or Ed25519 — determines how a subscriber verifies.

signing_public_key.description: Public verification key for the asymmetric algorithms. Absent for HMAC.

WebhookSubscriptionInput.description:
Body for creating an outbound webhook, transcribed from
`outbound_webhooks.CreateInput`.

This schema listed three properties, one of which (`active`) the create
handler does not accept — so a client following the contract could set a
field that was silently dropped, and could not discover the six the
endpoint really takes. `list_id` is the one that matters most: without
it every subscription is tenant-wide, and a caller reading this schema
had no way to know per-audience scoping existed.

algorithm.description:
Signing scheme. Empty defaults to hmac_sha256, so existing clients
keep working.

auth_config.description: Outbound auth for the receiving endpoint. Secrets are redacted on read.

filter_expression.description: Non-executable filter DSL; deliveries not matching are skipped.

list_id.description:
Scopes the subscription to ONE audience: only `list.subscriber.*`
events whose payload list_id matches are delivered. Omitted means
tenant-wide, which is the legacy behaviour.

transform_template.description: Maps output field names to RFC 6901 pointers into the event body.

effectiveScopes.description:
Scopes this member's role currently grants, derived from
roles_permissions. Empty when the role has no grants.

isSelf.description:
True for the calling session's own row. Always false on the
API-key path, which has no user identity.

callerIsOwner.description:
Whether the caller may grant the owner role. Lets a client
disable the control instead of surfacing a 403 afterwards.

auditAlertInboundBearer.description:
Route-specific shared secret stored in an audit alert rule's
`channel_config.inbound_secret`. It authenticates an external incident
callback and resolves its tenant; it is not a Moosewave API key or
dashboard session credential.

bearerAuth.description: Production bearer credential for scoped Moosewave API keys, marketplace OAuth access tokens, and short-lived stream tokens.

conversionSiteKeyBearer.description: Public pwk_ conversion site key sent in Authorization. This tenant routing/write identifier may be shipped in browser code; it is not a dashboard API key, read credential, or proof of conversion integrity.

conversionSiteKeyQuery.description: Public pwk_ conversion site-key fallback for clients that cannot set Authorization. Prefer the Bearer form where practical because query strings can appear in browser history, referrers, and infrastructure logs. A Bearer value takes precedence when both are supplied.
conversionSiteKeyQuery.name: key

pipedriveOAuthBasic.description: Pipedrive provider callback authentication using the configured OAuth app client ID and client secret.

portalCookie.description: Dedicated, tenant-bound, read-only audit-portal session. It is minted only by the one-time bootstrap exchange and is not interchangeable with dashboard or API-key credentials.
portalCookie.name: __Host-pw_audit_portal

realtimeStreamTokenQuery.description:
Two-minute `pws_` token minted by POST /api/v1/streams/token and
accepted only on the explicit realtime/download allowlist.
realtimeStreamTokenQuery.name: stream_token

sessionCookie.description: Secure HttpOnly dashboard session. Routes that declare only this scheme reject API keys and other machine credentials.
sessionCookie.name: pw_session

signedConversionHMAC.description:
Server-to-server conversion authentication. The header is
`keyid=<live key id>,v2=<lowercase HMAC-SHA256 hex>`. The HMAC binds
the key id, `X-Postwave-Timestamp`, and the exact raw request bytes;
the corresponding signing secret never travels over HTTP. This is not
a dashboard bearer token, session, tenant header, or publishable
conversion site key.
signedConversionHMAC.name: X-Postwave-Signature

tenantHeader.description: Required only for local-dev tenant resolution; ignored in production when the bearer credential carries tenant scope.
tenantHeader.name: X-Tenant-Slug

info.description:
Moosewave is the AI-native email platform: voice-modeled sequence
generation, deliverability intelligence, and dry-run verified ESP migration.

This document is the wire contract between the Moosewave gateway and
every first-party client (web app, CLI, SDKs). All four backend
services (`migration`, `voice`, `deliverability`, `automation`) are
fronted through the gateway at `https://api.moosewave.com`.

Production API clients authenticate with a scoped bearer token. Operations
that are intentionally browser-only override this default with the secure
dashboard session cookie. `X-Tenant-Slug` is a disabled-by-default local
development aid and is never a production authentication alternative.

post.description:
Resolves the workspace and server-owned policy version from a public
site key, then atomically appends the essential, analytics, and
marketing events for one pseudonymous visitor decision. The site key
is a public routing identifier, not a dashboard credential. Send it in
`X-Postwave-Site-Key` where possible; the body `site_key` and query
`site_key` forms are compatibility fallbacks.

A client should generate one high-entropy `Idempotency-Key` for each
user decision and retain it for transport retries. Concurrent and later
exact retries return the original decision and event UUIDs with
`Idempotent-Replayed: true`; reuse with different normalized visitor,
choice, analytics, marketing, or GPC semantics returns 409. Resolver
policy changes, IP addresses, and user agents do not create a false
mismatch. A keyed 202 echoes the exact validated `Idempotency-Key` as
`idempotency_key`; clients must verify that binding before deleting a
durable pending decision. Keyless requests remain temporarily accepted, are marked
`idempotent: false`, and return deprecation headers, but cannot recover
an ambiguous response after a transport failure.

`Sec-GPC` is strict: it must be absent or appear exactly once with the
value `1`. An affirmative signal overrides the body choice and denies
analytics and marketing. Without that header, `accept` requires both
category preferences to be true, `reject` and `gpc` require both to be
false or omitted, and `custom` may carry a mixed pair. Any supplied
essential/analytics/marketing value must be a JSON boolean and supplied
`essential` must be true; contradictory evidence returns 422 before any
row is written. The endpoint accepts only strict JSON, rejects unknown
fields and trailing values, and limits the encoded body to 16 KiB. Every
response is private/no-store.

parameters.description: Preferred public site-key transport. It takes precedence over every compatibility fallback.
parameters.name: X-Postwave-Site-Key

parameters.description: Compatibility site-key transport. Prefer X-Postwave-Site-Key because URLs can be logged.
parameters.name: site_key

parameters.description:
One exact, non-empty UTF-8 value of at most 255 bytes without
surrounding whitespace, control characters, or Unicode format
controls. Omission is supported only for legacy callers and makes
ambiguous retry recovery impossible.
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

parameters.description: The standardized affirmative Global Privacy Control signal. Duplicate or non-`1` values are rejected.
parameters.name: Sec-GPC

202.description: All three category events committed atomically, or the exact keyed decision was replayed.

Deprecation.description: Present with value `true` when a legacy keyless request was accepted.

Idempotent-Replayed.description: Present with value `true` only when an existing keyed decision supplied the response.

Warning.description: Present on a keyless success to explain that keyless public consent writes are deprecated.

post.description:
Records one server-to-server conversion from the exact raw JSON bytes.
This authenticates the source system and is separate from the
publishable `pwk_` browser beacon at `/api/public/track/conversion`.
Authentication does not by itself prove that the asserted outcome or
recipient identity is true.

Authentication is a key-bound version-2 HMAC. Let `key_id` be the live
conversion-signing key identifier and `timestamp` be current Unix
seconds. Sign these exact bytes with HMAC-SHA256 and the corresponding
signing secret:

`UTF8("postwave-conversion-v2\n" + utf8ByteLength(key_id) + "\n" + key_id + utf8ByteLength(timestamp) + "\n" + timestamp) || raw_body`

Send `X-Postwave-Signature: keyid=<key_id>,v2=<lowercase hex MAC>` and
the same timestamp in `X-Postwave-Timestamp`. The timestamp must be
within five minutes of the API clock. The secret is never sent. The
globally unique live key id resolves the tenant before a tenant-scoped
transaction begins; dashboard bearer/session auth and tenant headers
are neither required nor used by this operation.

`email_hmac_sha256` is derived with this exact signing secret over the
normalized email address. Resolution uses the exact key's indexed
tenant/key/digest projection. When that projection is not `ready`, a
request containing email-HMAC identity returns the closed 503
`email_identity_projection_not_ready`; it never scans subscribers or
silently records a false no-match. Requests using click or external
event identity do not depend on the email projection.

`Idempotency-Key` is mandatory and tenant-scoped. An exact retry with
the same raw body replays the original status and response bytes; reuse
with different bytes returns 409. Conversion facts and the replay
receipt commit atomically. The request is limited to 2 MiB and receives
the configured shared public IP abuse limit (10 requests per 60
seconds). Responses never include a tenant identifier and are never
cacheable.

202.description: Conversion and replay receipt committed, or the original exact response replayed.

400.description: Closed JSON, identity, event, money, or idempotency validation failed.

401.description: Signature is absent, malformed, unknown, invalid, or outside the replay window.

409.description: The same tenant/idempotency key was already used with different raw request bytes.

413.description: Raw body exceeds 2 MiB.

429.description: Configured public IP abuse limit exceeded.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds until the fixed window resets.

500.description: Conversion transaction failed without exposing internal or tenant detail.

503.description: Distributed public rate-limit storage is unavailable, or this exact key's email-HMAC identity projection is not ready; no conversion or replay receipt was attempted.

post.description:
Batch form of `POST /api/public/conversions/ingest`. Authentication,
exact raw-body signing, replay fencing, required idempotency, atomic receipt,
cache and public IP abuse-limit semantics are identical. The complete
batch commits in one tenant-scoped transaction. Empty batches and
batches above 500 are rejected; no prefix is partially accepted. The
receipt never includes a tenant identifier. If any item uses
`email_hmac_sha256`, this exact key's indexed identity projection must
be `ready`; otherwise the entire batch fails closed with 503 before a
conversion or replay receipt is attempted.

202.description: Entire batch and replay receipt committed, or original exact response replayed.

400.description: Closed JSON, empty batch, identity, event, money, or idempotency validation failed.

401.description: Signature is absent, malformed, unknown, invalid, or outside the replay window.

409.description: The same tenant/idempotency key was already used with different raw request bytes.

413.description: Raw body exceeds 2 MiB, or the batch contains more than 500 conversions.

429.description: Configured public IP abuse limit exceeded.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds until the fixed window resets.

500.description: Conversion transaction failed without exposing internal or tenant detail.

503.description: Distributed public rate-limit storage is unavailable, or this exact key's email-HMAC identity projection is not ready; no conversion or replay receipt was attempted.

post.description: Accepts a Postmark/SES-style JSON envelope through a signing proxy. The signature is hexadecimal HMAC-SHA256 over the exact bytes of `<timestamp>.<raw-body>` and the timestamp must be within five minutes. A stable event id (or signed payload MessageID) is atomically claimed before route matching, forwarding, fanout, classification, or mirroring. Exact retries return 202 without repeating side effects; identity reuse with different raw bytes returns 409.

post.description: Verifies a v2 HMAC-SHA256 that authenticates the normalized timestamp, normalized stable event identity, and exact raw body. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed from the two header values before the signed frame is built. The signed bytes are `v2:<timestampByteLen>:<timestamp>:<eventIdByteLen>:<eventId>:<rawBody>`; lengths are decimal UTF-8 byte lengths of the normalized values. The timestamp must be within five minutes and a stable event identity is mandatory. The identity is atomically claimed with durable trigger/automation intents. Exact retries return 202 without repeating completed side effects; identity reuse with different processed bytes returns 409. Raw-hex legacy v1 timestamp.body signatures are disabled unless a self-hosted operator explicitly enables the temporary migration switch.

parameters.description: Current Unix seconds. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed before this value is included in the signed payload.
parameters.name: X-Postwave-Timestamp

parameters.description: `v2=` followed by hexadecimal HMAC-SHA256(endpoint secret, canonical length-delimited timestamp/event-id/raw-body frame).
parameters.name: X-Postwave-Signature

parameters.description: Stable provider delivery id (maximum 512 bytes). Its value after trimming surrounding whitespace is authenticated by the v2 signature. Required unless X-Event-Id, X-GitHub-Delivery, X-Linear-Delivery, or X-Stripe-Event-Id supplies that identity.
parameters.name: X-Postwave-Event-Id

while `offers.PublicResolutionAvailable=false`; the dormant content

get.description:
Resolves a recipient-specific signed option without any durable write.
A GET never records or counts a response, including
when an email security gateway fetches every option. For a two-step
poll, the returned confirmation form contains a short-lived, randomly
nonced, self-contained signed credential required by POST. JSON remains the compatibility default for
empty, wildcard-only, or JSON-preferred `Accept` values. HTML is served
only when an explicit `text/html` range is actually preferred; that
representation is a script-free review form whose hidden `c` field is
the one-time challenge and whose action preserves the signed `r`/`t`
query. Neither representation counts a response. The response never
renders a raw email or returns a tenant id, recipient reference,
recipient hash, or token as a separate field.

404.description: Token, recipient reference, poll, or option is unknown; these cases are deliberately indistinguishable.

500.description: The signed preview could not be resolved.

post.description:
Records a confirmation for the signed recipient/option pair. For a
two-step poll, `c` is accepted either as the compatibility query
credential or as the sole field in a bounded
`application/x-www-form-urlencoded` browser submission. It is required,
expires after fifteen minutes, and is idempotently single-use. Each
distinct POST stores an immutable attribution receipt carrying the
exact revision, token key/time provenance, and bounded F01 evidence. Only an
explicit human classification may produce `state=counted`; missing,
unknown, or invalid classifier output is retained as
`unclassified_excluded`. Machine traffic is retained as
`machine_excluded`. Confirming multiple distinct options within the
guard window voids the affected responses as `voided_multi_option`.
A different option confirmed after that window supersedes the prior
current choice, so one recipient contributes at most one counted vote.
This endpoint returns the resulting state instead of claiming every
accepted POST was counted. JSON remains the default for empty,
wildcard-only, or JSON-preferred `Accept` values. When explicit HTML is
preferred, the endpoint returns a script-free result page directly
with the same status and a truthful counted, excluded, or voided
message; it does not redirect or render raw email/tenant identifiers.

parameters.description: Short-lived one-time preview credential required only when `two_step_required` is true.
parameters.name: c

c.description: Short-lived one-time credential minted by the HTML preview.

requestBody.description: Optional bounded browser form. No tenant, recipient, poll, option, or display content is accepted from the body.

text/html.example:
Response confirmed

Your response has been counted.

200.description: Confirmation persisted; inspect `state` and `counted` for the actual outcome.

400.description: The bounded confirmation form is malformed or too large; no response was recorded.

404.description: Token, recipient reference, poll, or option is unknown; these cases are deliberately indistinguishable.

409.description: The response can no longer be accepted in its current form.

428.description: The one-time preview credential was missing, expired, replayed, or otherwise no longer current; these states are intentionally combined.

500.description: Confirmation evidence could not be persisted.

post.description:
Mailbox-provider receiver for RFC 8058 `List-Unsubscribe-Post`. The
canonical request is form encoded as `List-Unsubscribe=One-Click`; for
compatibility, the bounded handler also accepts those literal bytes
case-insensitively when a smaller provider omits or changes Content-Type.

A valid request atomically activates the recipient suppression,
appends exactly one canonical consent-revocation event for that
suppression activation, and persists the subscriber-unsubscribed
webhook intent. Exact retries are successful no-ops; an active legacy
suppression missing its canonical event is healed once under lock.
Topic projection is a non-authoritative best-effort mirror.

This mandatory receiver is deliberately mounted outside the shared
10/min/IP public bucket because mailbox providers fan out unrelated
recipients through shared egress. Abuse is bounded by the opaque
recipient capability, a 1 KiB body ceiling, one indexed token lookup,
and the idempotent transaction. Every handler response is
`Cache-Control: private, no-store`.

schema.description: Must contain the case-insensitive literal `List-Unsubscribe=One-Click` marker.

requestBody.description:
RFC 8058 form body. The raw compatibility representation is accepted
for providers that send the same literal marker without the standard
media type. The entire encoded body, including any ignored fields,
must be at most 1,024 bytes.

post.description:
Accepts pre-identification activity without creating or resolving a
subscriber. The tenant is resolved from the request Host through a
verified custom domain. Supplying source_event_id makes retries
idempotent for that tenant and anonymous_id; otherwise each request
creates a new event.

202.description: The event was accepted, including idempotent duplicates.

400.description: The Host or anonymous_id is missing, or the JSON body is malformed.

401.description: The tracking Host does not resolve to a verified tenant domain.

413.description: The request body exceeds 64 KiB.

422.description: anonymous_id exceeds the supported 512-character bound.

get.description: Persists one tenant-bound conversion and returns a 1×1 transparent GIF. GET is the query-only `` integration: `event` defaults to `conversion`, and amount/properties are unavailable on this form. Authenticate with a public conversion site key in `Authorization: Bearer ` or `?key=`. A Bearer value takes precedence over the query fallback. The key identifies the tenant and grants conversion insertion only; it is intentionally publishable and does not prove that the submitted recipient, revenue, properties, or attribution claim is trustworthy. `c` is a best-effort campaign hint, followed by the `pw_campaign` cookie. Invalid, stale, missing, and foreign-tenant hints are persisted safely as unattributed (`campaign_id` omitted, `attributed_via=none`) without disclosing campaign existence. Every accepted request creates a new fact; this public endpoint has no idempotency contract. It shares one operational anti-abuse bucket with the remaining legacy public-route group: 10 requests per 60 seconds per resolved client IP. That shared ceiling is not a capacity or availability commitment and traffic to sibling public routes consumes the same bucket. All image/gif handler responses carry `Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate`. A cross-origin `` can use GET without CORS access; this contract does not grant a browser origin permission to read the response.

200.description: Conversion persisted; transparent pixel returned.

Cache-Control.description: Pixel responses are never cacheable.

401.description: The site key is missing, invalid, or revoked. Pixel callers still receive the transparent GIF bytes with status 401.

422.description: The query event or email fails conversion validation. GET always returns the transparent GIF representation with status 422.

429.description: The shared public-route IP bucket exceeded 10 requests in 60 seconds.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until this shared IP bucket resets.

500.description: Conversion persistence failed. Pixel callers receive the transparent GIF bytes with status 500; internal details are not disclosed.

503.description: The conversion tracker or shared rate-limit store is unavailable. Tracker failures preserve the pixel representation; a rate-limit store failure returns the standard JSON error envelope.

get.summary: Record a conversion through a tracking pixel

post.description:
Persists one tenant-bound conversion from browser or server-side JSON.
A non-empty body must be `application/json` or an
`application/…+json` subtype, may specify only a UTF-8 charset, and is
limited to 64 KiB. An empty body remains valid for query-only
compatibility. Non-empty body email, event_name, and campaign_id
values take precedence over equivalent query/cookie values; unknown
JSON fields are ignored.

Authenticate with a public conversion site key in
`Authorization: Bearer <pwk_…>` or `?key=<pwk_…>`. A Bearer value takes
precedence over the query fallback. The site key is a publishable
tenant-routing/write identifier, not a secret that protects revenue
integrity or proves subscriber identity.

`campaign_id` in the body wins over `c`, which wins over the
`pw_campaign` cookie. Attribution is best effort. Invalid, stale, or
foreign-tenant campaign hints do not fail or leak existence; the
conversion persists unattributed with `attributed_via=none`.

The normal representation is JSON. `Accept: image/*` selects the same
transparent-pixel response used by GET, including for handler errors.
Every image/gif handler response carries
`Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate`.
Every accepted request creates a new fact; there is no idempotency or
deduplication contract.

This route shares the legacy public-route anti-abuse bucket of 10
requests per 60 seconds per resolved client IP. The limit is shared
with sibling public routes and is not a production throughput or
availability claim. Browser fetch integrations are same-origin unless
the deployment explicitly allows their origin through CORS; the public
site key itself does not grant cross-origin response access.

requestBody.description: Optional conversion JSON. An entirely empty body uses query/cookie values; any non-empty body must use a supported UTF-8 JSON media type.

execution. Offer actions are release-held and absent from the current
catalog: the dormant decline receipt primitive is not a recipient-bound
producer or mounted customer action surface, and acceptance would
complete a purchase without certified release/refund machinery.

exists only in the agent's memory and as a hash here.
