refused: a key that could mint a mandate would let an agent grant itself
authority, and a self-issued bound is not a bound. The property that
makes this governance is that a mandate always traces to a person.

immediately preceding window, then asks the configured LLM to interpret
server-computed aggregates. The LLM cannot author SQL. Revenue evidence
is scoped to one deterministic dominant ISO 4217 currency selected over
the combined comparison horizon (revenue sum descending, conversion
count descending, currency code ascending); every returned total, daily
point, and campaign row uses only that currency. `revenue_scope`
discloses the selected currency and how many other currencies were
excluded. When no monetary conversions exist, its currency is null and
all revenue evidence is explicitly zero/empty.

human+machine+unknown figure, which is the historical behaviour and
is unchanged. `unknown` covers every interaction that predates the
classifier or that the cascade could not settle, and is never folded
into `human`: counting unclassified traffic as human is the exact
assumption the classifier exists to stop being made silently.
The band constrains opens and clicks. Deliveries and bounce counts
are rate denominators that carry no engagement classification and
are never filtered by it.
parameters.name: classification

of the cohort month. Only weeks completed by every subscriber in the
monthly cohort are emitted, so newer cohorts have shorter arrays and

get.description:
Walks the `supersedes_id` lineage for one campaign and one explicit time
window and reports WHAT THE CLASSIFIER CHANGED, separately from what the
audience did.

This is the read the append-only design exists for. Reclassification
appends a superseding verdict rather than overwriting, so the earlier
one remains auditable — but a lineage that is written and never read is
only bookkeeping. Without this endpoint a customer whose human-engaged
reach moved cannot tell whether their AUDIENCE changed or the
CLASSIFIER did, and those are opposite conclusions that the headline
number alone cannot distinguish.

`restated_events` counts verdicts a newer classifier re-confirmed and is
reported separately from `changed_events`: a reclassification that
agreed with itself is evidence of stability, and folding it into the
changed count would make an unchanged verdict look like churn.
`unlinked_multiple_verdict_events` counts events carrying more than one
verdict with no lineage link between them — reported rather than
guessed at, because inferring an order would invent the very history
this endpoint exists to record.

get.description:
The downloadable form of the reclassification delta. It answers the
question asked after the number moves, usually by somebody who was not
in the room: "you told me my reach changed and that it was your
classifier rather than my audience — show me." A dashboard figure cannot
be attached to a procurement review or a dispute; a digest-addressed
file can.

The window must be stated explicitly, as it must for the reach evidence
export: a defaulted window would produce a file whose digest depended on
WHEN it was downloaded, which defeats addressing it by digest at all.

The embedded SHA-256 identifies the normalized evidence payload and
`Content-Digest` covers the exact downloaded bytes. Both detect
accidental modification; neither is a Moosewave signature and neither
proves authenticity.

The artifact states what it does NOT observe as prominently as what it
does: it holds the recipient population fixed and varies only the
classifier, so movement beyond the figures reported here is audience
movement and is not measured by this document.

downloaded bytes. The vendor `+json` representation is kept
uncompressed even when the request advertises gzip or Brotli, and no
`Content-Encoding` field is emitted. These digests detect accidental
modification but are not a Moosewave signature and do not prove
authenticity. Persistence,
supersession lineage, and delta-to-prior-artifact history are not part
of this synchronous export contract.

approving session. The client must keep it in memory and echo it on
session-grant `approve` or `deny`; switching account, workspace, or
session requires a new inspection. API-key decisions do not require
this token. Omitting `action` retains the legacy CLI behavior and means
`approve`, so existing API-key approval clients remain compatible.

`grant_kind` for the legacy CLI API-key flow. A session flow returns a
high-entropy `device_code` that must remain only on the requesting
device; the QR/verification URL contains only the short user code.
Target-device identity is derived from transport headers, never from a

post.description:
The requesting device polls with its private `device_code`. Pending,
slow-down, denial, and expiry use RFC 8628 error codes. An approved
API-key grant returns the key once and remains a one-shot legacy
exchange. An approved session grant atomically creates a short-lived,
provisional `pw_session` cookie and returns
`confirmation_required: true`; that cookie is not accepted by normal
authenticated endpoints. The target must immediately call this same
endpoint with `action: confirm`, the same in-memory `device_code`, and
the exact provisional cookie. Confirmation is idempotent and activates
the tenant-capped session lifetime.

A retried session poll during the short recovery window replays only
the exact same bound cookie; it never creates a second session. A
retried confirmation likewise returns the already-activated session.
`action: cancel` is idempotent for an already-cancelled grant and also
revokes the exact session created by a consumed session grant. Omitting
`action` retains the legacy polling behavior.

Present on a successful session poll/replay or confirmation.
Poll sets the exact provisional cookie; confirmation resets
that same cookie to its activated browser or persistent
lifetime. Cancellation also expires the cookie when the
request presents the exact session bound to that grant; it
never clears an unrelated signed-in session.

request; or confirmation without the exact provisional cookie.

Lists every workspace (tenant) the authenticated user belongs to,
marking the active one, so the shell workspace switcher can offer a
switch. Read-only — switching happens via the existing
login(workspace_id) re-auth flow.

post.description:
Mints a session in another workspace the authenticated user's email
belongs to, WITHOUT a credential re-entry, and revokes the calling
session. Replaces the sign-out + `login(workspace_id)` round trip that
made an in-app workspace switcher impossible on mobile.

Refused with `email_not_verified` unless the CALLING session's user row
has proven mailbox control (`email_verified_at` set, or an
auth_provider that verified it: google / microsoft / saml /
magic_link). Signup issues a live session before the verification email
is answered, so without that guard an unverified signup under someone
else's address would be a takeover of their existing workspace.

The new session is deliberately NOT MFA-satisfied: the target tenant's
MFA policy re-challenges exactly as it would a fresh password login.
Switching into the workspace the session is already in is a 200 no-op
with `switched: false` and does not rotate the session.

Keep-me-signed-in, mirroring the login flag. Defaults to
false (short-lived browser-session cookie).

`email_not_verified` (the calling session has not proven mailbox
control) or `workspace_access_revoked` (the membership is
suspended or deleted).

404.description:
The email does not belong to that workspace. Deliberately
indistinguishable from a workspace that does not exist.

path visit link an outcome to a campaign, but cannot identify who
redeemed a forwarded code or prove that anyone read the message.

currencies; an empty item currency means the historical unit was not
retained and must be shown as unavailable.

snapshot. A missing or tenant-foreign campaign returns `404`; it is never
represented by an authoritative-looking empty register.

coupon-allocation release gate. It does not create or release inventory.

Authoring is authenticated and tenant-scoped even though the path it produces is public: minting a link that assigns revenue credit is an authoring act. The response states `attribution_scope: campaign` and `attributed_via: campaign_vanity_path` so whoever publishes the link knows what it will and will not prove BEFORE they print it anywhere — a vanity path is shared by every recipient and can be reposted publicly, so it is evidence about the campaign and never about which person visited. interval, `event: delta` whenever the underlying counts change.
An initial or later lookup failure is logged internally, emitted as a
stable `event: error` payload, and closes the stream without disclosing
the producer error. Heartbeat comments arrive every 30s to keep the
connection alive across proxy idle timeouts.

The stream ends when the client closes the connection or the
server shuts down. Clients should reconnect with EventSource's
built-in auto-reconnect.

status or an internal diagnostic.

source—verifies every referenced block against the current source tree.

validator are mandatory. Weak, wildcard, list, padded, missing, or stale
validators never weaken into an unconditional write. A successful
response returns the updated campaign and its next strong ETag. The
mutation is bounded to 256 KiB and is private/no-store.

code, without requiring a preceding click. This is outcome-linkage
evidence, not proof of who presented the code or who read the campaign:
a code can be forwarded, copied, or shared. The response therefore says
`attribution_scope: campaign_assignment` and
`readership_proven: false` explicitly.

matches. Shared/static or reused codes fail closed with `ambiguous_code`;
supply the opaque `assignment_id` returned by allocation to disambiguate.
Render keys are never accepted as redeemable codes.

Exactly one `Idempotency-Key` is required. For 24 hours, replaying the
exact method, target, body, authenticated principal scope, tenant and key
returns the original status, headers and bytes. Reusing the key with a
different request returns 422; an in-flight duplicate returns 409 and
never records a second outcome.

cause signed requests containing email-HMAC identity to fail closed
with `503 email_identity_projection_not_ready`; they never silently
degrade to an unmatched identity. Revoked keys retain their last

post.description:
Mints one tenant-owned HMAC signing key. The plaintext secret appears
exactly once in this `no-store` response and cannot be recovered;
persist it only in the calling system's secret manager and never log
it. An omitted body, `{}`, or an empty label is accepted. A non-empty
body is strict JSON and is limited to 1 KiB.

`Idempotency-Key` MUST NOT be sent. This credential-reveal operation is
excluded from the durable replay ledger, must never be retried
automatically, and its plaintext response cannot be replayed or
recovered. After an ambiguous transport result, list key metadata,
identify any newly issued key ID, revoke it, and issue a replacement;
never retry issuance blindly. Every response, including authentication,
authorization, validation, routing, and server-error outcomes, carries
`Cache-Control: private, no-store` at the root response boundary.

A new key is returned with `identity_projection_status=pending` and a
non-null `identity_projection_updated_at`. It must not be presented as
email-HMAC-ready until a later list response reports `ready`. Session
callers must complete the immediate step-up challenge; an admin-scoped
API key does not receive an interactive challenge.

conversions, cryptoshreds its stored ciphertext, erases retained HMAC
fact/touch evidence for that key, and removes its email-HMAC bindings
and pending projection work. The lifecycle row and destruction receipt
remain for incident review. Missing, tenant-foreign, and already-revoked ids return the same
non-disclosing 404. Rotation is overlap-first: issue a replacement,
wait for its projection to report `ready`, move callers, then revoke
the old key.

post.description:
Mints a new public conversion site key. The plaintext is disclosed
by the logical create operation; subsequent key-list reads expose only
its prefix. An omitted body, `{}`, or an empty label uses `web`.
Labels are trimmed, limited to 120 Unicode characters, and reject
control characters. A non-empty body is strict JSON, rejects unknown
fields, accepts only `application/json` or an
`application/…+json` subtype using UTF-8, and is limited to 64 KiB.

Site keys are designed to be shipped in browser code. They grant only
tenant-bound conversion insertion and do not read tenant data.

Idempotency-Key is optional. Without it, every successful call mints a
distinct key. With it, the authenticated tenant-wide idempotency layer
stores 2xx and 4xx responses for 24 hours. Repeating the exact method,
target, and raw body with the same key replays the original status,
headers, and bytes instead of minting another site key; changing the
request returns 422 and an in-flight duplicate returns 409.

This means the plaintext 201 body remains recoverable for up to 24
hours by an exact retry or an administrator using the idempotency
inspector/replay surface. Treat the Idempotency-Key and cached response
as sensitive: use a high-entropy, operation-unique value and never log
either plaintext. Once the record expires, lost plaintext cannot be
recovered; create a replacement and revoke the old key.

get.description:
Returns every custom-domain row owned by the authenticated tenant,
newest first, as a raw JSON array. The production route-authorization
family requires an `admin` API-key scope or an admin-capable dashboard
role even though the package-level list handler does not add another
scope wrapper.

This endpoint is intentionally not paginated. The first-party desktop
decoder fails closed when a response contains more than 500 domains;
the API repository does not currently enforce that client-side limit.
Every response emitted after the handler is entered carries
`Cache-Control: private, no-store, max-age=0`.

post.description:
Creates an unverified tenant-owned custom domain and returns its CNAME
and TXT ownership challenges. Input is strict JSON: unknown fields,
multiple JSON values, malformed JSON, non-JSON media types, and bodies
over 32 KiB are rejected. `application/json` and registered
`application/*+json` media types are accepted; the only permitted media
type parameter is `charset=utf-8`, and a missing Content-Type is a 415.

Registration is fail-closed and disabled in the current production
composition until automated TLS issuance and renewal, authoritative
dependency inventory and teardown, and production routing are
qualified end to end. After authentication and admin authorization,
that gate is
evaluated before the request body is decoded; while disabled, every
request therefore receives the documented 503 capability response,
even when its body is otherwise invalid. A 201 response is possible
only in an explicitly enabled composition. Creating a row or later
verifying its DNS challenges does not issue a certificate, configure
edge routing, or activate traffic for the hostname.

Every response emitted after the handler is entered carries
`Cache-Control: private, no-store, max-age=0`.

composition until automated TLS issuance and renewal, authoritative
dependency inventory and teardown, and production routing are
qualified. The gate is evaluated after authentication and admin
authorization but before row lookup or DNS resolution, so the current
authorized response is 503 even for an unknown identifier.

When explicitly enabled, this performs a fresh CNAME/TXT lookup for
every persisted challenge record, using one shared five-second lookup
context, and atomically stores the latest record results. No request
body is consumed. Verification can regress from true to false; any
failed later check clears the persisted verification timestamp so stale
ownership does not remain current.

`verified=true` means only that every currently persisted DNS challenge
matched during this check. It does not mean that TLS was issued, edge
routing exists, traffic is active, or the hostname is otherwise ready
to serve. Every response emitted after the handler is entered carries

get.description:
Computes a tenant-isolated rollup for a trailing one-to-365-day window.
Counts are receiver-reported aggregate message counts, not individual
messages. Alignment means SPF or DKIM passed according to the ingested
aggregate record. Receiver disposition values describe reported DMARC
policy actions; they do not prove inbox placement or final delivery.

An omitted `domain` produces a tenant-wide rollup and the response
carries an empty `domain` string. `latestPolicy`, when present, is only
the `p=` value observed in the newest in-window report for an explicitly
selected domain. It is historical report evidence, not the currently
published DNS record, and must not be presented as a safe replacement
TXT value. `topSources` and `topFailingSources` are independently capped
at ten; `sourceCount` and `sourceListTruncated` disclose completeness.
Daily series entries exist only for reporting days that contributed a
positive message count.

After authorization has entered the handler, every success or error
response is marked `Cache-Control: private, no-store, max-age=0`,
`Pragma: no-cache`, and `Expires: 0`. Authentication, authorization,
and rate-limit middleware can reject the request before those
handler-local headers are applied.

parameters.description:
Optional exact policy-domain filter. Clients should send the
canonical lowercase ASCII form; omission selects tenant-wide data.
parameters.name: domain

parameters.description: Length of the trailing evidence window in 24-hour periods.
parameters.name: days

200.description: Aggregate alignment, disposition, source, series, and qualified suggestion evidence.

400.description:
`domain` is invalid, `days` is not an integer from 1 through 365,
or an unknown/repeated query parameter was supplied. Stable codes
include `invalid_domain`, `invalid_days`, and `invalid_query`.

get.description:
Returns a newest-first, tenant-isolated page of minimized DMARC
aggregate-report summaries plus an explicit completeness receipt. This
is receiver-supplied aggregate evidence: it is not a live DNS lookup,
inbox-placement measurement, final-delivery receipt, or forensic-message
feed. Raw XML, reporting-contact email addresses, tenant identifiers,
and per-recipient data are deliberately omitted.

`domain` is an optional canonical ASCII hostname. `from` includes a
report when its reported range ends on or after the timestamp; `to`
includes a report when its range begins on or before the timestamp.
When both are present, `from` must not be later than `to`. The response
is capped by `limit` and `meta.hasMore`; no cursor or offset is exposed.
`meta.availableDomains` is a separate tenant-wide inventory capped at
500 entries and reports its own truncation flag.

After authorization has entered the handler, every success or error
response is marked `Cache-Control: private, no-store, max-age=0`,
`Pragma: no-cache`, and `Expires: 0`. Authentication, authorization,
and rate-limit middleware can reject the request before those
handler-local headers are applied.

parameters.description:
Optional exact policy-domain filter. Clients should send the
canonical lowercase ASCII form; the handler trims surrounding
whitespace and lowercases otherwise valid input.
parameters.name: domain

parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound applied to report-range end time.
parameters.name: from

parameters.description: Inclusive upper bound applied to report-range begin time.
parameters.name: to

parameters.description: Maximum summaries returned; this endpoint has no offset or cursor.
parameters.name: limit

200.description: Bounded report summaries and exact scope/completeness metadata.

400.description:
A query value is invalid. Stable codes are `invalid_domain`,
`invalid_from`, `invalid_to`, `invalid_limit`, `invalid_window`,
and `invalid_query`. Unknown or repeated query parameters are
rejected rather than silently ignored.

get.description:
Returns a tenant-isolated aggregate summary for one canonical IPv4 or
IPv6 source plus up to 200 contributing report rows, newest first.
`summary` covers the complete in-scope source aggregation even when
`perReport` is capped; `hasMore=true` discloses that the per-report
evidence list is incomplete. This endpoint does not identify a sender
owner, classify authorized versus unauthorized traffic, expose raw XML,
or prove inbox placement or final delivery.

An omitted `domain` selects this IP across all tenant report domains;
the response then omits `domain`. The time window is the same trailing
one-to-365-day, 24-hour-period model as the insights endpoint.

After authorization has entered the handler, every success or error
response is marked `Cache-Control: private, no-store, max-age=0`,
`Pragma: no-cache`, and `Expires: 0`. Authentication, authorization,
and rate-limit middleware can reject the request before those
handler-local headers are applied.

parameters.description: Canonical IPv4 or IPv6 source address to inspect.
parameters.name: ip

parameters.description: Length of the trailing evidence window in 24-hour periods.
parameters.name: days

200.description: Complete source summary and a bounded per-report evidence receipt.

400.description:
`ip` is missing or invalid, `domain` is invalid, or `days` is not
an integer from 1 through 365. Unknown or repeated query parameters
are also rejected. Stable codes include `invalid_ip`,
`invalid_domain`, `invalid_days`, and `invalid_query`.

post.description:
Reserved administrative mutation for a future durable, attributable,
reviewable suggestion-audit model. It is intentionally unavailable in
the production composition: after authentication, authorization, and
tenant resolution, the handler returns
`503 suggestion_acknowledgements_disabled` before decoding a body or
touching persistence. A 200 response is documented only to make the
dormant wire shape reviewable; it is not production-reachable and must
not be treated as a released capability.

If a separately qualified composition explicitly enables the dormant
path, it accepts one strict JSON object no larger than 4 KiB, rejects
unknown fields and multiple JSON values, permits only a suggestion code
emitted by the current insight rules, and limits the optional note to
1,000 UTF-8 bytes without control characters. Repeating the same code
updates that acknowledgement. This dormant behavior is not a substitute
for the missing actor identity, history, expiry, review, and policy-
version semantics required before production enablement.

Every response emitted after handler entry is marked
`Cache-Control: private, no-store, max-age=0`, `Pragma: no-cache`, and
`Expires: 0`. Authentication, authorization, and rate-limit middleware
can reject the request before those handler-local headers are applied.

200.description:
Dormant idempotent acknowledgement result. This is reachable only
in a separately enabled, non-production-qualified composition.

400.description: The explicitly enabled dormant handler rejected JSON syntax, shape, code, or note content.

413.description: The explicitly enabled dormant handler received more than 4 KiB.

415.description: The explicitly enabled dormant handler requires a supported UTF-8 JSON media type.

500.description: The explicitly enabled dormant persistence operation failed.

503.description:
Normal authorized response in the production composition. The
durable suggestion acknowledgement model is not release-qualified,
so no request body is decoded and no acknowledgement is persisted.

delete.description:
Reserved administrative inverse of the dormant acknowledgement
mutation. It is intentionally unavailable in the production
composition: after authentication, authorization, and tenant
resolution, the handler returns
`503 suggestion_acknowledgements_disabled` before validating the code
or touching persistence. A 200 result is documented only for review of
the explicitly enabled dormant path; it is not production-reachable
and must not be advertised as a released capability.

Every response emitted after handler entry is marked
`Cache-Control: private, no-store, max-age=0`, `Pragma: no-cache`, and
`Expires: 0`. Authentication, authorization, and rate-limit middleware
can reject the request before those handler-local headers are applied.

200.description:
Dormant idempotent removal result. This is reachable only in a
separately enabled, non-production-qualified composition.

400.description: The explicitly enabled dormant handler rejected the suggestion code.

500.description: The explicitly enabled dormant persistence operation failed.

503.description:
Normal authorized response in the production composition. The
durable suggestion acknowledgement model is not release-qualified
and no persisted acknowledgement is removed.

get.description:
Retrieves the current representation exposed by `GET /api/v1/emails`.

`attempt_state` narrows to one lifecycle state. The one that matters
operationally is `unknown`: a send whose provider outcome could not be
established — a transport failure after the request was written, where
the provider may have accepted the message and no receipt exists to say.
Those are never retried automatically, because neither re-sending nor
discarding is safe, so this is how an operator finds them.

parameters.description:
Filter by lifecycle state. `prepared` (claimed, provider not yet
called), `submitted` (provider accepted), `rejected` (provider
refused; safe to retry), `unknown` (outcome not establishable;
needs a human).
parameters.name: attempt_state

200.description: The recent transactional sends for this tenant.

post.description: Send a single transactional email (Resend-style). `from` defaults to the tenant's configured sender; `to`/`cc`/`bcc`/`reply_to` accept a string or an array; one of `html`/`text` is required. Supports custom headers, per-message tags, attachments (base64 `content` or remote `path`), and `scheduled_at` for delayed delivery. Suppressed recipients are skipped. Honors the Idempotency-Key header.

202.description:
Accepted — returns {id, status, suppressed?}. Always a 2xx even when
the dispatch itself failed: the outcome is reported in `status` and
`error`. A 5xx here would make the idempotency middleware treat the
attempt as transient and DROP its claim, so a retry would be free to
send the message a second time.

When an Idempotency-Key was supplied, a replay returns the ORIGINAL
send's id and its real status. A previous attempt that the provider
refused outright is retried; one that reached the provider, or whose
outcome could not be established, is not.

409.description:
The supplied Idempotency-Key was already used for a DIFFERENT
message (code `idempotency_key_reused`). Neither answer available
without this status is acceptable: a 2xx returning the first
message's id would silently discard the second, and a 5xx would let
the middleware drop the claim and re-send.

502.description: The message failed to dispatch (body carries the error).

post.description:
Send up to 100 distinct emails in one call. Body is a bare array or
{emails:[...]}. Returns {data:[{id,status}]} with one result per email.

An Idempotency-Key is applied PER POSITION (`<key>:<index>`), because one
key for the whole batch would make the second message a replay of the
first and silently drop it. A retry that reorders the batch therefore
finds each position holding a different message and reports
`status: "conflict"` for those members rather than sending them.

200.description: {data:[SendEmailResult]}

post.summary: Send a batch of transactional emails

get.description:
Every declared version, newest first per event — not just the active one.
The point of versioning is that events collected under an older
declaration can still be explained, and a list hiding the old rows makes
that impossible.

`violation_count` is how a tenant sees their app and their declaration
disagreeing. It is a count with one recent example rather than a row per
event: a drifting app would otherwise write one per event, and the
question being asked is "is this declaration still true".

200.description: Declared schemas for this tenant.

post.description:
Creates a NEW version and makes it active. Never edits in place: editing
a declaration rewrites the meaning of events already collected under it,
and the violation count on the row would then describe two different
contracts added together.

Declaring does not reject events. A property whose type moved is still a
usable event, and dropping real customer data because an app shipped a
change is worse than the drift — so violations are counted and the
event is stored.

Reads the tenant's retained append-only event log in ascending sequence

RFC 3339 TIME cursor, for a client resuming a dropped SSE
connection. The live payload carries `at` but no sequence_id,
because the log writer is a best-effort hook whose failures are
deliberately swallowed so it cannot take the stream down -- so a
streaming client has no sequence to resume from, only a timestamp.

stream is cache invalidation, which is idempotent, so a duplicate
costs one redundant refetch while a miss costs permanently stale
data.

post.description: Enables source-event polling where the source adapter supports it, for pilot shadow-mode drift detection. Customer.io is explicitly unsupported because its App API exposes no complete incremental profile-change feed; use a frozen final full snapshot and post-delta shadow check instead. ActiveCampaign, HubSpot, and Klaviyo pilot acceptance verifies fresh pre-delta replay evidence when the monitor was enabled before final delta. HubSpot events poll changed contacts only. They do not prove standalone list-membership or preference-only changes, hard deletions, loss/change of an email address, current-email eligibility after an unobserved change, or current exact membership; one CRM Search window fails closed at 10,000 results. Retain continuous overlap evidence, poll more frequently/narrowly when needed, and use the frozen final full snapshot as authority. Klaviyo events poll changed primary-email profiles only, request predictive_analytics under its stricter 10 requests/second and 150 requests/minute tier, and preserve the last full-snapshot suppression-filtered send-targetable audience projection. They do not prove deletions, secondary email identities, per-address consent, raw membership, or current list/segment membership and never replace the final full snapshot. Replay fails closed on a stable-profile email A-to-B move while the prior source-owned A destination remains active; the full snapshot must materialize B and disable A before replay resumes.

Customer.io evidence must cover global/channel/topic preferences and ESP suppressions, immutable-cio_id and duplicate-email ownership, profiles without email, frozen segment/topic membership, workflow/transactional/non-email rebuilds, deliverability, and ecosystem dependencies. Klaviyo consent/suppression and ecosystem evidence must account for the mandatory multi-email identity/per-address-consent review record, suppression-filtered rather than raw audience membership, nullable flow/draft-message definitions, and IDs-only campaign tags. Klaviyo acceptance also requires the mandatory secondary-email/per-address-consent source-archive record, full-snapshot resolution of any fail-closed stable-profile email move, suppression-filtered audience review, and nullable-definition/IDs-only-tag review. Its eight static product-area rows are unconditional checklists rather than detected inventory; it treats flows as rebuild-only, sent email campaigns as archive-only, and reports, SMS runtime/consent continuity, and ecommerce as out of scope.

post.description: Create a migration job from credential-based source auth. Customer.io requires an App API key in `api_key` (never a Track API site key), `extra.region` set to `us` or `eu`, and `account_id` (or the low-level `extra.customerio_workspace_id` alias) when the key exposes multiple workspaces. The job is bound to the exact region/workspace returned by `/v1/workspaces`; an unrolled-back tenant/workspace lineage must reuse its original job for credential refreshes and full-snapshot deltas. Klaviyo accepts either a private API key in `api_key` or a caller-managed OAuth bearer in `access_token`, validates `/accounts`, and requires `account_id` or `extra.klaviyo_account_id` when the credential exposes multiple accounts; the resulting job is bound to that exact account. Bearer handoff does not start or manage a migration OAuth flow: the caller owns authorization, refresh, and revocation, distinct from the native Klaviyo integration's managed OAuth lifecycle. An unrolled-back Klaviyo tenant/account lineage must reuse its original job. ActiveCampaign requires both `api_key` as the API token and the account API URL in `account_id` or `extra.api_url`. HubSpot uses the private app token in `api_key`, validates the current portal identity, accepts an optional numeric hub ID in `account_id` or `extra.hub_id`, and durably binds the job to that exact portal; refresh cannot silently switch portals. Beehiiv uses an API key and accepts the publication ID in `account_id` or `extra.publication_id`, which is required when the key can access multiple publications. Part of the ESP/CRM import / migration flow.

For Klaviyo this is the account ID returned by `/accounts` and is required when the key exposes multiple accounts. For ActiveCampaign this may be the account API URL from Settings -> Developer. For Beehiiv this is the `pub_...` publication ID and is required for a multi-publication workspace.

HubSpot's delta is an idempotent full contact/list/preference/eligibility snapshot and is authoritative for current-primary-email identity, fields/status, hard removals, loss/change of email, exact list/subscription membership, and conservative current-email eligibility; changed-contact polling cannot prove standalone list/preference changes or deletions. Customer.io has no supported incremental profile-change feed, so every commit/delta is a complete email-addressable immutable-`cio_id` snapshot that reconciles duplicate-email ownership, email moves/deletions, authoritative status/fields, and exact frozen memberships. Klaviyo changed-profile polling likewise cannot prove deletions or list/segment membership, so its final delta is a fresh full source snapshot.

post.description: Pre-flight inventory of what's in the source account. Mailchimp can be called first without a selection to enumerate audiences, then with explicit selected_audience_ids to inventory the intended audience-bound scope. HubSpot discovery exactly inventories email-addressable and excluded non-email contacts, additional email identities, non-sensitive property definitions/populated values, exact list inventory/version/membership with only allowlisted structural list metadata, active email subscription definitions, per-contact/wide preferences, and current-primary-email eligibility. HubSpot filter predicates are deliberately not requested or persisted because their operations can contain sensitive property and integration-event literals; operators must inspect and rebuild, retain, or retire those rules in HubSpot. Enabled requires every active definition SUBSCRIBED, no scoped/wide opt-out, and no hard-bounce, quarantine, invalid-address, non-marketing/unknown-marketing-contact, pending/unconfirmed double-opt-in, or legacy-opt-out restriction. This is conservative import eligibility, not exact HubSpot sendability parity; current-email changes require a fresh full snapshot. HubSpot fails closed above 1,000,000 contacts, 10,000 traversal pages, 64 MiB retained snapshot data, a 10,000-result changed-contact search window, or a daily API budget that cannot cover one probe, two preference reads per email-addressable contact, and max(1,000 calls, 5% of daily limit) reserve. Customer.io discovery is bound to one selected region/workspace and exactly inventories email-addressable immutable-cio_id profiles, profiles without usable email, frozen segment/topic membership, campaigns/broadcasts/newsletters, Design Studio templates, object-type metadata, global/channel/topic preference evidence, ESP suppressions, and explicit rebuild/archive checklists. Sent email newsletters become campaign archive only with at least one explicit `language=""` default and provably composable source HTML. The lowest stable content ID represents a multi-default/A-B set with an explicit warning, all variants remain source evidence, and translations are never silently selected. A missing or empty layout uses the exact non-empty source body with a fidelity warning; a non-empty layout must contain exactly one documented `{{content}}` slot. Newsletter and Design Studio HTML are exact source content/composition, not provider-rendered output; Liquid, CSS/assets, components/styles/transformers, and per-recipient rendering require destination validation. Campaigns and broadcasts remain workflow definitions. API-broadcast trigger evidence retains only trigger IDs plus created/processed timestamps; original trigger payloads, audiences, and per-user data are not returned and require manual reconciliation. Transactional/non-email definitions remain rebuild evidence rather than executable imports. Klaviyo discovery snapshots the primary email identity and available consent/suppression state from stable Get Profiles, the exact enumerated send-targetable list/segment projection after validated list-level suppressions are excluded, flow definitions, forms, templates, sent-email campaign inventory, non-email source-archive evidence, and a mandatory multi-email identity/consent review record. The adapter does not expose separate raw Klaviyo membership counts. Stable Get Profiles does not expose secondary email identifiers or independent per-address consent/suppression, so discovery cannot certify complete profile identity or consent parity. Klaviyo profile reads request predictive_analytics and are throttled to its stricter 10 requests/second and 150 requests/minute tier; nullable list/segment names receive deterministic Klaviyo list <id> and Klaviyo segment <id> fallbacks. Draft campaign-message and flow definitions may be null and remain explicitly incomplete rebuild evidence; campaign tag relationships preserve provider IDs only, not resolved names. Eight static product-area source-archive rows are emitted unconditionally as checklists: source_total=1 means one checklist record, not detected source inventory. Flows remain rebuild-only and only sent email campaigns become email archive rows. Part of the ESP import / migration flow.

post.description:
Admin-only live diagnostic that performs at most one immediate, signed
HTTP POST to the endpoint's current real receiver URL. The receiver may
mutate downstream state. This is not a preview, queue, or automatic
retry surface, and the TypeScript/Python SDKs and MCP adapter
deliberately do not wrap arbitrary custom-payload fire.

The caller must mint and retain one canonical `fire_id` and one exact
`Idempotency-Key` for the logical fire, and submit the positive
`expected_webhook_config_version` that the operator confirmed. The
server atomically snapshots that exact destination/configuration,
applies its filter and transform, and durably reserves the fire
identity before contacting the receiver.
An exact same-key retry returns the frozen inspection receipt even when
the webhook was edited or paused later. A key/body mismatch returns
422. A pending same-identity request returns 409 and must be reconciled
through `GET /api/v1/outbound-webhooks/playground/fires/{fire_id}`;
never mint a new identity merely because the caller cancelled or lost
the POST response.

`filtered` proves the receiver was not contacted. Any received HTTP
response, including 4xx/5xx, is represented by `receiver_responded` in
a 200 inspection receipt. `transport_ambiguous` and status_code 0 mean
the receiver may have processed the request even though Moosewave saw no
response. Receiver credentials and credential-like URL, header, body,
response, error, and oversized partial-response values are redacted or
withheld. Session callers require a current step-up; admin-scoped API
keys do not receive an interactive challenge.

Use synthetic data only; do not submit customer personal data or
secrets. The credential-redacted request inspection and bounded receiver
response are still potentially personal arbitrary content. Moosewave
stores the exact inspection receipt in an envelope-encrypted private
record under the tenant's webhook-delivery retention policy. Conventional
email-shaped identifiers support a literal-email locator query. Its
synchronous section returns only the newest 100 matches, includes no
aliases, and has no continuation. A direct-ledger erasure helper can
match the requested address and current known aliases, but the public
erasure path remains disabled by the repository-wide coverage gate.
Names, phone numbers, or other identifiers without that email are not
discoverable. Retention cryptoshredding removes the receipt ciphertext,
receipt digest, and email locators. The permanent payload-free control
row retains tenant/fire/webhook identity, configuration revision, event
type, state/outcome/status/timestamps, and idempotency/request hashes as
the no-redispatch fence. Access-bundle JSONB copies are outside this
receipt lifecycle; this is not a complete subject access or erasure
control.

426.description: A recognized first-party client is below its configured minimum version.

get.description:
Exact tenant owner/admin sessions and exact tenant-bound admin-scoped
API keys only. Returns independent active authority facts at one
monotonic visibility revision, newest first, with canonical UTC
response-observation metadata. `nextCursor` is opaque, tenant-bound,
filter-bound, and snapshot-bound; callers must continue explicitly and
must not interpret a page as current complete history. Row evidence
timestamps can be later than `snapshotAt` after database clock rollback.
The API returns only a 16-character display fingerprint, never a raw
device token or its full SHA-256 digest. The send gate is fail-closed,
but customer omnichannel runtime qualification, audience
materialization, and live APNs/FCM provider execution remain
release-held; registry presence does not claim that a live send ran.

parameters.description: Exact customer push platform; omitted means all platforms.
parameters.name: platform

parameters.description: Exact authority reason; omitted means all reasons.
parameters.name: reason

parameters.description: Exact 8–16 lowercase-hex prefix of the minimized display fingerprint.
parameters.name: hash_prefix

parameters.description: Canonical unpadded base64url continuation returned by the preceding page for this exact tenant and filter set.
parameters.name: cursor

parameters.description: Canonical decimal page size; malformed, repeated, signed, or zero-padded values are rejected.
parameters.name: limit

200.description: One strict tenant-bound page at a stable monotonic visibility revision, with response-observation metadata.

get.summary: List one private push-suppression snapshot page

x-postwave-private-response.appliesTo: all outcomes, including exact-admin authentication and authorization refusals

post.description:
Creates only an independent reversible `manual/dashboard` authority
fact for the exact tenant, platform, and raw token bytes. It cannot
mint provider, user-opt-out, complaint, or legacy authority and does
not normalize APNs or FCM tokens. A stable optional `Idempotency-Key`
makes transport retries replay-safe; the unique authority tuple also
makes an unkeyed exact reassertion return the existing row.

200.description: The exact manual authority already existed and was reasserted without changing provenance.

201.description: A new independent manual authority fact was created.

422.description: Token, platform, or reason is semantically invalid; no authority fact was created. Malformed, unknown-field, trailing, or null JSON is a 400.

post.summary: Add or reassert one manual push hold

x-postwave-private-response.appliesTo: all outcomes, including exact-admin authentication and authorization refusals

post.description:
Validates 1–100 unique `(platform, exact raw token bytes)` entries and
commits every manual authority fact plus one aggregate audit record in
one transaction. Any invalid, duplicate, storage, or audit outcome
rolls back the entire batch. Input and receipt item order are identical.
A stable optional `Idempotency-Key` makes ambiguous transport retries
replay-safe.

200.description: All entries were committed or reasserted atomically.

422.description: Batch size, duplicate identity, token, platform, or reason is semantically invalid; nothing was committed. Malformed, unknown-field, trailing, or null JSON is a 400.

post.summary: Atomically add or reassert manual push holds

x-postwave-private-response.appliesTo: all outcomes, including exact-admin authentication and authorization refusals

post.description:
Compare-and-swap removes 1–100 unique manual/dashboard authority rows
in one transaction. Every id and `expected_version` must still match;
locked, missing, stale, duplicate, audit, or storage failure rolls back
the entire batch. Each receipt says whether another independent active
authority still suppresses the same token. A stable optional
`Idempotency-Key` makes ambiguous transport retries replay-safe.

200.description: Every reviewed manual authority was removed atomically.

422.description: Batch size, duplicate id, id, or expected version is semantically invalid; nothing was committed. Malformed, unknown-field, trailing, or null JSON is a 400.

post.summary: Atomically remove reviewed manual push authorities

x-postwave-private-response.appliesTo: all outcomes, including exact-admin authentication and authorization refusals

delete.description:
Compare-and-swap removes only the exact active manual/dashboard row at
`expected_version`. Provider, user-opt-out, complaint, and legacy facts
are review-locked. Success does not imply the token became sendable:
`stillSuppressed=true` means another independent authority remains.
A stable optional `Idempotency-Key` makes ambiguous retries replay-safe.

200.description: Exact versioned removal receipt, including remaining-authority truth.

422.description: The id or expected version is invalid; no authority was removed.

delete.summary: Remove one reviewed manual push authority

x-postwave-private-response.appliesTo: all outcomes, including exact-admin authentication and authorization refusals

Clients should load this no-store preflight before enabling the

post.description:
Compile a plain-English audience description into the canonical
SegmentNode AST. Two engines are selectable via the `engine`
query-param:

  * `engine=rules` (default) — deterministic phrase compiler.
    Covers ~20 common audience descriptions (tier/plan, tags,
    country/language, open/click recency windows, cold/never
    engaged, new joiners, churn risk, high-value/CLV, RFM
    champions, SMS consent, status, email domain). Returns 422
    `unsupported_text` when the phrase matches no pattern. Clients
    must not silently retry through an external AI provider.

  * `engine=ai` — LLM fallback (ai_segment_compiler). Validates
    every predicate against the per-tenant registry and every
    time-window against the documented grammar, and returns a
    `nutrition_facts` explainability payload (inferred predicates,
    time windows, source) plus an `ai_processing` disclosure with
    factual provider/model metadata when available. Retention and
    residency remain `not_declared` unless a future verified policy
    source can assert them. Returns 503 `ai_unavailable` when no AI
    provider is configured. Every AI request must include
    `ai_processing_acknowledged: true`; the server rejects a missing
    per-request external-processing choice. The AI branch is also
    protected by the distributed very-expensive tenant rate limit;
    rules mode is not charged against that bucket. Use the GET
    preflight on this same path before enabling AI.

Operates on saved subscriber segments.

ai_processing_acknowledged.description: Required and true when engine=ai; ignored by rules mode.

ai_processing.description: AI engine only. Honest processing disclosure.

Creates one tenant-owned rule and returns its canonical projection,
including the initial `updated_at` mutation revision. Omitted `active`
defaults to true; omitted or empty `channels` defaults to email. A
stable optional `Idempotency-Key` binds the exact method, path, and raw
body for 24 hours. For keyed creates, the rule, audit evidence, and
byte-exact 201 replay receipt commit in the same tenant transaction, so
retrying after an ambiguous acknowledgement cannot create a second rule.

delete.description:

carry the rule's current `updated_at`; omission fails with 428 and a
stale valid revision fails with 409. The delete and its audit evidence
commit in one transaction.

204.description: Rule and its transactional audit evidence committed; no response body.

Idempotent-Replayed.description: Present as true only when the exact 204 response was restored from the 24-hour replay ledger.

409.description: The rule revision changed, or an exact keyed request is still resolving; nothing new was deleted.

428.description: The required `expected_updated_at` precondition was omitted.

x-postwave-private-response.appliesTo: all outcomes, including pre-handler authentication and authorization refusals

patch.description:

JSON body must carry the current `updated_at`; omission fails with 428
and a stale valid revision fails with 409. A successful write returns a
strictly advanced `updated_at` and commits its audit evidence atomically.

200.description: Updated canonical rule carrying its advanced revision.

Idempotent-Replayed.description: Present as true only when the exact 200 response was restored from the 24-hour replay ledger.

409.description: The rule revision changed, or an exact keyed request is still resolving; nothing new was updated.

428.description: The required `expected_updated_at` precondition was omitted.

patch.description:
Applies a partial update through `PATCH /api/v1/settings/notifications`.

Notifications are governed by a category × channel matrix. Each category
(`send_complete`, `approval_request`, `bounce_alert`,
`deliverability_alert`, `usage_alert`) can be delivered over three
independent channels:

- `email_on_*` — the account email address.
- `inapp_on_*` — the in-app notification feed plus web/mobile push.
- `webhook_on_*` — an outbound POST to `notification_webhook_url`
  (Slack-compatible `{ "text": ... }` payload). The webhook channel only
  fires when the per-category flag is on **and** a URL is configured.

Every field is optional; an omitted field preserves the stored value.
`notification_webhook_url` sends an empty string to clear the destination
or a URL to set it (validated as an https public host — private,
reserved, and localhost destinations are rejected).

200.description: The updated notification preferences.

get.description:
Returns the exact tenant-owned hourly cap, quiet-hours policy, legacy
fallback projection, mutation revision, and (when resolvable) sending-IP
pool. This private control plane is exact-admin; all outcomes, including
authorization refusals, are emitted with `Cache-Control: private, no-store`.

x-postwave-private-response.appliesTo: all outcomes, including pre-handler authentication and authorization refusals

put.description:
Replaces the tenant's hourly cap and quiet-hours policy. Supplying
`expected_updated_at` performs an exact compare-and-set: an empty string
asserts first write, an RFC3339 value asserts the loaded revision, and a
stale assertion fails with typed 409 without changing settings or audit
evidence. A cap-changing request also fails with typed 409 while an
automatic Deliverability Hub repair owns the installed cap; cap-preserving
quiet-hours changes remain valid. Omission retains the legacy
unconditional-write contract.

`Idempotency-Key` MUST NOT be sent. This cap-control operation is
excluded from the generalized replay ledger because a 503 can mean the
durable mutation committed while shared cap coordination remains
conservatively fenced, or that the commit outcome is still unknown.
Attempt it once, inspect the exact outcome, and refresh authoritative
sending-settings and cap-coordination state before any further action.

The mutation-outcome header is a phase receipt, not a default inferred
from the HTTP status. A 401, 403, or 413 can be produced before this
handler runs and therefore can omit the header. A recovered 500 can
likewise omit it, or retain any exact phase value established before
the failure. Only an explicitly received `not-committed` value proves
that another attempt is safe without read-only reconciliation; an
absent or different value is ambiguous and MUST NOT trigger a replay.

200.description: Canonical committed settings carrying the new mutation revision.

x-postwave-private-response.appliesTo: all outcomes, including pre-handler authentication and authorization refusals

Recurring cron and duration-based drip inputs are rejected because the worker does not durably re-arm a refreshed source or enforce an exact reviewed duration. Only valid while status='preview'. auto_create_properties is the import's "create new custom fields" choice: when the workspace custom-field mode is auto, mapped keys the workspace has not declared are created as text fields when the import runs. An unconfirmed upload (status preview) is discarded: it becomes 'cancelled' at once, and its uploaded file and review data are purged on the next worker tick instead of after the 24-hour abandoned-preview window. Send expected_status "preview" to discard only: the call then never stops an import that was already confirmed, and answers 409 not_a_preview with the import untouched.

For a one-time scheduled row, the response includes scheduled=true + next_scheduled_at and the worker holds the row until it is due. Legacy cron or non-zero drip settings are rejected with 409 until cleared. SUB-105: a {"dry_run": true} body instead runs a validation-only pass — every row is classified (create / update / skip / fail) with no writes, the per-row outcomes are returned in dry_run_results, and the row stays in 'preview' for a later real confirm. Custom-field columns are judged under the workspace's custom-field mode (GET /api/v1/custom-fields/mode) exactly as the worker will apply it. A row whose address carries an erasure tombstone (the contact was deleted or erased by a privacy request) fails with error_code erasure_blocked in the dry run and again when the import runs; such an address is never re-created.

patch.description:
When a subscriber's detected jurisdiction shifts into a stricter consent
regime (e.g. US→EU), jurisdiction_reconfirm_required is set on the
profile. This endpoint atomically records the subject's complete evidence
envelope in both the subscriber receipt ledger and canonical consent-event
ledger, projects email-channel consent, applies the accepted/declined
subscriber state, clears the flag, and appends the audit record. Any
failed write leaves the flag and consent state unchanged. The expected
jurisdiction-change timestamp and exact strong subscriber version must
come from the same reviewed detail response and form the one-time
compare-and-swap precondition. This binds the legal copy to the canonical
email and complete profile state the operator actually reviewed. An exact
semantic retry returns the already-committed subscriber without adding
evidence, while stale, email-rotated, conflicting, or
server-regime-mismatched attempts return 409. Write-subscribers scope.

expected_subscriber_version.description: Exact strong Subscriber.version from the same reviewed detail response. Wildcard, weak, malformed, or synthesized validators are rejected before any evidence is written.

privacy_policy_version.description: Reviewed privacy-policy version persisted in both consent ledgers; limited to 100 UTF-8 bytes and 100 Unicode scalar values.

regime.description: The reviewed regime; it must match the server classification for the detected jurisdiction.

200.description: Updated subscriber after both consent ledgers, projections, flag, downstream sync intent, and audit record commit, or the same current subscriber on a verified exact retry. The body version is fresh and jurisdiction_reconfirm_required is false.

ETag.description: Exact strong revision of the returned Subscriber; always identical to body.version.

409.description:
State/precondition conflict. Stable error codes are
jurisdiction_reconfirmation_not_required,
jurisdiction_reconfirmation_stale,
jurisdiction_reconfirmation_regime_mismatch, and
jurisdiction_reconfirmation_state_invalid.

server-side event filter: filtering happens before cursor evaluation,

precedence over the legacy `before` timestamp when both are present.
The statistics remain an overall unbounded subscriber rollup and are
intentionally independent of the event category and current page.

get.description:
Returns the explicit open/click opt-out evidence and the effective
decisions used at send time. `effective_open_opt_out` and
`effective_click_opt_out` include Global Privacy Control: when `gpc` is
true, both are true even if the corresponding timestamp is absent. A
successful send-time preference lookup with no stored row permits
tracking; a lookup error suppresses both tracking modes while delivery
remains available. The response is private/no-store. Its body `version` is the exact
token for the next PATCH If-Match precondition; privacy middleware
strips the ETag cache validator.

patch.description:
Locks the current subscriber identity and atomically commits the tracking
preference projection, one canonical `email_tracking` consent event per
changed evidence dimension, mandatory audit evidence, and a durable
`subscriber.consent_changed` webhook-fanout intent. Any failed write
rolls the entire transaction back. `Sec-GPC: 1` forces `gpc=true` and
evidence source `gpc`; GPC suppresses both open and click tracking.
One strong If-Match token from the latest GET is mandatory. Missing,
wildcard, weak, unquoted, or multi-value preconditions return 428. A
conflicting stale token returns 412; an exact semantic retry succeeds
without duplicating events, audit rows, or outbox intents even when it
carries the original token.

parameters.description: The exact body `version` returned by the latest GET. Exact semantic retries are idempotent even with the original token.
parameters.name: If-Match

parameters.description: A value of `1` forces gpc=true and evidence source=gpc regardless of body values.
parameters.name: Sec-GPC

post.description:
Persists one Product Event for an existing subscriber in the
authenticated tenant. This is a live write, not a preview or sandbox:
after the event commits it can fan out to matching automations and
flow runs, and order-shaped events can feed revenue attribution.

Identify the subscriber with `subscriber_id` or `email`. When both are
supplied, `subscriber_id` is authoritative. The JSON body is limited
to 1 MiB, unknown fields are rejected, and `event_name` must use the
canonical lowercase dot-delimited snake-case grammar. Omitting
`occurred_at` uses the server's current UTC time.

Supplying an optional `Idempotency-Key` makes ambiguous retries safe.

`occurred_after` is an inclusive RFC3339 lower bound: an event exactly
at that instant is included. The server captures one upper `asOf`
instant before reading, executes the lookahead and row scan in one
repeatable-read snapshot, and excludes future-dated occurrences after
that instant. The frozen scope prevents concurrent inserts from making
the truncation signal disagree with the streamed rows.

clamped cap is returned in `X-Postwave-Export-Limit`.
`X-Postwave-Truncated: true` is present only when another matching row
exists beyond that cap. Both headers are CORS-exposed. Export
responses are private and non-cacheable.

Opens a tenant-scoped Server-Sent Events stream for Product Events
persisted after the connection is established. The server first reads
the current maximum durable event id. If that bootstrap read fails, it
returns 500 before opening the stream; historical rows are never
replayed as if they were live.

A successful connection emits one `hello` event whose JSON data is
`ProductEventStreamHello`, then emits `track` events whose JSON data is
`ProductEvent`. The server polls every two seconds, sends heartbeat
comments every 20 seconds, and advances its durable cursor even when an
`event_name` filter excludes a row. Transient polling failures keep the
connection open. Clients should treat reconnects as a fresh live tail,
not as a complete history transport.

must hold both reporting and subscriber-read authority.

Resolves, normalizes, and de-duplicates at most 250,000 addresses,
persists the complete item set, and queues a durable asynchronous
verification job. `inline` and `upload` carry addresses in `emails`;
`tag` resolves one tenant tag named by `source_ref`; and
`all_subscribers` resolves the tenant's subscriber pool. Omitting
`source` selects `inline`. A `202` response proves only that the
durable job and its items were accepted; this request does not call a
verification provider.

Exactly one `Idempotency-Key` is mandatory. It is an exact opaque
request identity, used exactly as supplied; surrounding whitespace is
invalid. During the shared 24-hour tenant/principal replay window, an
exact method, path, query, key, and byte-identical body replay the
original `202` response. A concurrent exact request returns `409` with
`Retry-After`; different request bytes return `422`. Independently, the
durable job binds the tenant-scoped key to the normalized source,
execution mode, and resolved address set so retries cannot authorize
different billable work.

The bulk-execution capability is fail-closed. When it is disabled the
handler returns the typed `verification_bulk_unavailable` `503` at
handler entry, before resolving a source, creating a job, or starting
provider/worker work.

get.description: Returns unaccepted, unexpired invitations. Token hashes are never exposed.

200.description: Pending invitations.

post.description:
Mints a single-use, expiring invitation to join this workspace with a
fixed role. No email is sent — the plaintext token is returned exactly
once so the caller can compose the accept link; only its SHA-256 is
stored. Only an owner may invite at the owner role.

201.description: The invitation plus its one-time token.

409.description: The email is already a member (`already_member`) or has a pending invite (`invite_pending`).

delete.description: Deletes a pending invitation so its link can no longer be redeemed.

200.description: Revoked.

get.description:
Returns the people in the workspace with their role, lifecycle status
and the scopes that role currently grants. `GET /api/v1/roles` returns
role DEFINITIONS; this returns the humans those definitions apply to.

Soft-deleted members are hidden unless `include_deleted=true`.

parameters.description: Include soft-deleted members in the roster.
parameters.name: include_deleted

200.description: The workspace roster.

patch.description:
Updates a member's role and/or lifecycle status. Three invariants are
enforced: the workspace always keeps at least one active owner
(`last_owner`), only an owner may grant the owner role, and only an
owner may modify a sitting owner (`owner_role_required`).

`status` accepts `active` or `suspended` only. Hard deletion is the
account-deletion flow's job and is rejected here.

200.description: The updated member.

403.description: Only an owner may grant the owner role or modify a sitting owner.

409.description:
The change would leave the workspace without an active owner
(`last_owner`), or the member is soft-deleted and owned by the
account-deletion flow (`member_deleted`).

patch.summary: Change a workspace member's role or status
